candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If the operation involves the application of a material (a "coating") to plastic parts or products (including associated activities such as surface preparation, cleaning, mixing, and storage), then the operation falls within the source category covered by this subpart.

If the material applied is an adhesive (a chemical substance applied for the purpose of bonding two surfaces together), then that application is treated as a coating for purposes of this subpart (subject to specific exclusions in the definitions).

If you use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in the surface coating of plastic parts and products and the source is a major source (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP), then you are subject to this subpart.

If your surface coating or coating operation meets any of the exemption criteria listed in § 63.4481(c) (e.g., uses only coatings/thinners/cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, research/laboratory or hobby shop activities, specified product-specific exclusions), then that surface coating/operation is not subject to this subpart.
If the application is performed using handheld, non-refillable aerosol containers, touch-up markers, or marking pens, then that activity is not a coating operation for purposes of this subpart.

If the activities are part of the affected source (all coating operations as defined in § 63.4581 plus all storage, mixing, conveying equipment for coatings/thinners/additives/cleaning materials and waste handling), then they are within the scope of an affected source for this subpart.

If the equipment/operation was first constructed after December 4, 2002 according to the criteria in § 63.4482(c)(1)–(3), then the affected source is a new source (otherwise it may be existing or reconstructed), which affects which emission limits and requirements apply.

If the activity is limited to surface preparation or cleaning (use of a cleaning material/solvent to prepare a substrate or remove dried coating) and is not directly related to application of a coating, then that activity may not constitute a surface coating operation under this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the methylene chloride application is intended to bond parts (i.e., functions as an adhesive) or instead is only cleaning/surface preparation (check purpose, process description, and expected residue—does it leave a film or solids?).

Measure or estimate the annual volume of methylene chloride-containing materials and any other coatings/thinners/additives/cleaning materials used in these solvent-welding lines (liters or gallons per year).
Determine whether the methylene chloride-containing material and any other materials used contain organic HAP (use supplier formulation data, Method 311, or Method 24 as applicable).
Determine whether the facility is a major HAP source (potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/year total HAP); include emissions from these lines in that calculation.
Verify whether the application method is exempt (handheld non-refillable aerosol, touch-up markers, marking pens) or is an industrial coating/adhesive application (not exempt) per § 63.4481(a)(1).

Check whether any of the specific exemptions in § 63.4481(c)(1)–(17) apply to your operation (e.g., research/lab, hobby shop, only non-organic HAP coatings, product-specific NESHAP applicability overlaps).

Identify all equipment and activities that would be part of the affected source per § 63.4482(b) (coating operations, storage/mixing vessels, conveying equipment, waste handling) to determine scope of coverage.
If this is a new or modified installation, confirm construction/installation dates relative to Dec 4, 2002 and whether the criteria for a 'new' affected source in § 63.4482(c) are met.

If you plan to use a compliance alternative (predominant activity, facility-specific limit, or choose another surface-coating NESHAP where allowed), document and calculate the basis per § 63.4481(e) and § 63.4490.

candidates.title: Area-source NESHAP for Secondary Copper Smelters

criteria.criterion: If your facility processes copper scrap in a blast furnace and converter or uses another pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper from copper scrap (including low-grade scrap) and is an area source, then it is a secondary copper smelter and is subject to this subpart if it is a new affected source.

If your facility merely melts recycled copper scrap or copper alloy scrap to produce ingots or for direct use in a manufacturing process (and does not produce anode copper by pyrometallurgical purification), then it is not a secondary copper smelter and this subpart does not apply.
If the affected source commenced construction or reconstruction before October 6, 2006 then it is not a new affected source and the new-source provisions of this subpart do not apply.

candidates.title: Area-source NESHAP for Aluminum, Copper, and Other Nonferrous Foundries (Copper Foundries)

criteria.criterion: If your facility is a copper foundry that melts copper and pours molten copper into molds to manufacture complex-shaped copper castings (not including primary or secondary metal producers that cast simple shapes such as anode copper) and is an area source meeting the annual metal melt production (existing) or annual metal melt capacity (new) threshold of at least 600 tons per year, then this subpart applies.

If your operations are those of a primary or secondary metal producer that cast molten copper to produce simple shapes such as sows, ingots, bars, rods, anode copper, or copper cake, then the facility is not a copper foundry and this subpart does not apply to those melting/casting operations.

If you commenced construction or reconstruction of the melting operation after February 9, 2009, then determine applicability based on annual metal melt capacity at startup as described for new affected sources.

candidates.title: Area-source NESHAP for Secondary Nonferrous Metals Processing Facilities

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a secondary nonferrous metals processing facility that is an area source of HAP emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If you are an area source subject to this subpart, then you are (in general) exempt from the obligation to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 71 solely because of area-source status but must continue to comply with the subpart's requirements.

checklist: Does the facility process copper scrap using a pyrometallurgical purification process (e.g., smelting furnace, blast furnace, converter, or other melting/oxidation-reduction and fluxing steps) specifically to produce anode copper that is shipped off-site?
Does the facility cast molten copper into anodes (anode copper) rather than into complex-shaped castings (i.e., are final products anodes/ingots/simple shapes vs. castings)?
Is the furnace you operate a smelting furnace or melting furnace as described in the definitions (type: tilting anode furnace — characterize whether it functions as a pyrometallurgical smelter)?
Was the affected source constructed/reconstructed on or after October 6, 2006 (for Subpart FFFFFF new-source test) and/or on or after February 9, 2009 (for Subpart ZZZZZZ new-source test)?
Is the facility classified as an area source of HAPs (i.e., below major-source thresholds) under 40 CFR part 63 for the relevant HAPs?

What is the facility's annual metal melt production (if existing) or annual metal melt capacity at startup (if new) for copper and other nonferrous metals, in tons per year (to compare to 600 tpy and 6,000 tpy thresholds)?

What percentage and types of scrap are charged (confirm the 90% copper sorting and whether scrap contains oils, plastics, insulation, or other contaminants subject to the subpart's scrap-preparation work practice standard)?

Do you plan to capture and control furnace and transfer fumes with a capture system and control device (baghouse or other), and what PM control approach will be used (baghouse + bag leak detection vs alternate control device requiring approved monitoring plan)?
Will you be issuing/obtaining an operating permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 71 as required if subject to Subpart FFFFFF or otherwise required by permitting authorities?
Confirm whether any operations involve sweating or burning insulation or other non-melting scrap-prep activities (the facility reports none; verify in practice and in scrap pretreatment plan).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Perchloroethylene Dry Cleaning Facilities (Subpart M)

criteria.criterion: If a dry cleaning facility uses perchloroethylene (PCE), then the provisions of this subpart apply to the owner or operator.
If a dry cleaning system is located in a building with a residence after December 21, 2020, then the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of PCE from that dry cleaning system.

If a dry cleaning system was installed or relocated after December 21, 2005 and is located in a building with a residence, then the owner or operator must eliminate any emission of PCE from that system (per the post-2005 installation rule).
If you operate a coin-operated dry cleaning machine, then that machine is exempt from the requirements of this subpart (i.e., not subject to the subpart's requirements).

If the facility emits or has the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons per year) of PCE, or meets the specified yearly PCE consumption thresholds in §63.320(g), then the dry cleaning facility is a major source (otherwise it is an area source).

If the total yearly PCE consumption (calculated per §63.323(d)) is less than 530 liters (140 gallons) per year under the conditions in paragraph (d), then certain machines/facilities are exempt from many sections of §§63.322–63.324 as specified in §63.320(d).
If the facility includes only transfer machine system(s) and total yearly PCE consumption is less than 760 liters (200 gallons) per year, then certain exemptions apply as specified in §63.320(e).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source has a relevant standard established pursuant to section 112 of the Act, then the requirements in §63.6 apply to the owner or operator of that affected source.

If an existing source is subject to a standard established under this part, then the owner or operator shall comply with that standard by the compliance date established in the applicable subpart (and in no case will the compliance date established for an existing source exceed 3 years after the effective date of the standard).

If an affected source is subject to a relevant standard, then at all times the owner or operator must operate and maintain the source and associated control/monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

candidates.title: Subpart EEEE (general requirements — excerpts)

criteria.criterion: If equipment identified in §63.2338(b)(1)–(5) is in OLD operation, then you must be in compliance with the emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards in this subpart whenever that equipment is in OLD operation.

If you are subject to Subpart EEEE, then you must operate and maintain your affected source, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, according to §63.6(e)(1)(i) (unless and until paragraph (d) of §63.2350 changes that obligation per the listed compliance dates).

If you are subject to Subpart EEEE, then you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) plan per §63.6(e)(3) as required by this subpart, except as modified by the dates and exceptions in §63.2350(c)–(d).
If you are subject to Subpart EEEE, then Table 12 to that subpart identifies which parts of the General Provisions (§§63.1–63.15) apply to you.

checklist: Do you use perchloroethylene (PCE) in your dry cleaning operations?
Is the dry cleaning facility located in a building that includes any residence(s), including residences that are currently vacant? (see 40 CFR 63.324(f)(3))
Is the dry cleaning machine coin-operated?
What type of machine do you operate: dry-to-dry or a transfer machine system (washer + dryer/reclaimer)?

What is the date the dry cleaning machine was constructed, reconstructed, installed, or relocated (to determine whether it was installed/relocated after Dec 21, 2005 or other compliance-date triggers)?
What is the facility's total yearly PCE consumption (sum of purchases over the prior 12 months, calculated per 40 CFR 63.323(d))?
Based on yearly PCE consumption, does the facility meet any exemption thresholds (e.g., <530 L/yr per §63.320(d), <760 L/yr per §63.320(e)) or the major-source thresholds in §63.320(g)?
Do you currently eliminate PCE emissions during transfer and at door opening (e.g., refrigerated condenser and/or non-vented carbon adsorber configured per §63.322 and monitored per §63.323)?

Do you have monitoring and records required by §63.323 and the purchase/consumption logs and notification/recordkeeping required by §63.324 (including the notification in §63.324(f) identifying if the facility is located in a building with a residence)?

If subject to Subpart EEEE, is your equipment identified in §63.2338(b)(1)–(5) and are you following the General Provisions that apply (see Table 12 per §63.2398) and the SSM/operation requirements in §63.2350 and §63.6(e)(1)(i)?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Plants (NESHAP, Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a portland cement plant that is a major source or an area source, then this subpart applies to each kiln including inline coal mills.
If a coal mill uses kiln exhaust gases (i.e., is an in-line coal mill), then it is considered part of the kiln and is subject to the kiln emissions limits and monitoring requirements of this subpart.

If kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill that exhausts through a separate stack, then the combined PM emissions from the kiln and the coal mill stack are subject to the kiln PM emissions limit and must be accounted for in compliance calculations.

If kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill that exhausts through a separate stack, then initial and subsequent performance testing must include simultaneous testing of the kiln and coal mill stacks and calculation of the combined PM emission rate for each test run.

If subject to PM limits under this subpart, then initial compliance must be demonstrated using Method 5 or 5I and continuous compliance must be demonstrated by operating a PM continuous parametric monitoring system (PM CPMS) with annual (or required) performance tests and establishment of a site-specific operating limit.

If kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill that exhausts through a separate stack, then kiln-specific THC and HCl limits must be calculated using the flow-weighted equations that include the coal mill stack (and THC/HCl must be measured either upstream of the coal mill or in the coal mill stack) for establishing compliance limits.

If subject to mercury limits and kiln gases are diverted to a coal mill that exhausts through a separate stack, then you must account for mercury emitted from the coal mill by conducting performance tests on the coal mill/alkali bypass stacks (Method 29 or 30B as specified), develop hourly mercury mass emissions for those stacks, and sum kiln + coal mill emissions to determine the 30-day rolling average per clinker production while operating the required Hg CEMS or sorbent-trap monitoring system.
If an onsite source is subject to the standards for nonmetallic mineral processing plants in subpart OOO of 40 CFR part 60, then that onsite source is not subject to this subpart.

If the coal mill exhaust is commingled with the kiln exhaust in a single stack, then you may demonstrate compliance either by testing the commingled stream or by testing the kiln exhaust prior to reintroduction and separately testing the diverted stream and adding all emissions for each pollutant.

checklist: Is the facility a portland cement plant and is it a major source or an area source (per 40 CFR 63.2)?
Does the coal mill use kiln exhaust gases (i.e., does it meet the subpart LLL definition of an in-line coal mill) or does it have its own independent heat source?
Does the coal mill exhaust through a separate stack, or are its exhausts commingled with the kiln/clinker cooler exhaust before the PM control device?
If the coal mill has a separate stack: what are the stack flow rates (Qcm) and are there sampling ports for Method 5/25A/321/29/30B as needed?
Which air pollutants/limits apply at the kiln (PM, D/F, THC/total organic HAP, HCl, Hg) for this kiln (new vs existing, major vs area) per Table 1 in 63.1343?
What PM control device(s) serve the kiln and/or coal mill (baghouse/ESP/wet scrubber) and are control device inlets/outlets combined or separate?

Are there existing CEMS/CPMS: PM CPMS, THC CEMS, HCl CEMS or HCl/SO2 CPMS alternative, Hg CEMS or sorbent trap system, and are they installed upstream of the coal mill or at the coal mill stack as appropriate?
If demonstrating HCl or THC compliance, can you measure upstream of the coal mill or in the coal mill stack and do you have the necessary spans/calibrations per §63.1350(i)/(l)?
Is the coal mill (or any onsite equipment) already subject to an NSPS or subpart OOO of 40 CFR part 60 (nonmetallic mineral processing) that might exclude it from Subpart LLL under §63.1340(c)?

Can you operate/measure clinker production and stack flow continuously and with the accuracy required (weigh scales, flow monitors) to calculate lb/ton-clinker emissions and 30-operating-day rolling averages per §63.1350(d) and (n)?

Do you have the capability to perform simultaneous performance tests (Method 5/5I for PM, Method 25A for THC, Method 321 for HCl, Method 29/30B for Hg, Method 23 for D/F, Method 18/320 for organic HAP) on kiln and coal mill stacks and to calculate flow-weighted, combined emissions as required?

Are control-device parameter monitors (e.g., sorbent injection rate, carrier gas flow/pressure, scrubber pressure/pH, bag leak detection) installed and capable of meeting the CPMS requirements referenced in the subpart?
If relying on alternative monitoring (e.g., SO2 CEMS for HCl), have you prepared the data/information to support an alternate monitoring application per §63.1350(o)?

candidates.title: Area Source Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating (Autobody/Motor Vehicle and Target HAP coatings)

criteria.criterion: If you are an area source of HAP and you perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles and mobile equipment, then you are subject to this subpart.

If you are an area source of HAP and you perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to a plastic and/or metal substrate on a part or product (excluding facility maintenance or space vehicle), then you are subject to this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.11180 (Target HAP / Target HAP containing coating definition)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you spray apply no coatings that contain the target HAP and you submit the required petition or notification to the Administrator demonstrating you do not spray apply any target HAP-containing coatings, then you may be exempt from the surface coating provisions of this subpart (subject to Administrator verification).
citations: 40 CFR 63.11180 (Target HAP / Target HAP containing coating definition)

criteria.criterion: If your source is not an area source (i.e., is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP), then this area-source subpart does not apply.

If the surface coating or paint stripping meets any of the exclusions in §63.11169(d) (for example research and laboratory activities, quality control activities, or activities covered under another area-source NESHAP), then this subpart does not apply to those activities.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (Miscellaneous Metal Parts NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and that source is a major source (or is located at or part of a major source of HAP), then you are subject to this subpart.

If your coating operation uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (as determined under the referenced methods), then this subpart does not apply to your coating operation.

If coatings used in a given coating category are in volumes of less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under this paragraph does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then this subpart does not apply to those coating activities under that paragraph.

If your polyurea/spray line is part of the affected source as defined (all coating operations, storage, conveyance, and waste handling associated with surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products), then that line is included within the affected source scope for this subpart.

If your surface coating activity meets any of the other exclusions or product-specific exceptions listed in §63.3881(c)(2) through (c)(17) (for example product categories subject to other surface coating NESHAPs, certain web or coil coating processes, aerospace, shipbuilding, etc.), then this subpart does not apply for those activities.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source or a major source of HAP (calculate actual and potential HAP emissions vs. 10 t/yr single HAP or 25 t/yr total HAP).
For the polyurea spray line, determine whether coatings are spray-applied as defined (hand-held or spray gun atomizing device) and whether the substrates are metal or plastic.
Identify whether the polyurea line coats assembled motor vehicles or mobile equipment (autobody/mobile equipment) or miscellaneous metal parts/products that are not motor vehicles.

Obtain and review manufacturer formulation data / MSDS for the polyurea coating as received and determine whether it contains any target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd) at or above the thresholds in 40 CFR 63.11180 (>=0.1% for carcinogenic target HAPs (Cr, Cd, Pb, Ni) and >=1.0% for Mn).

If the polyurea coating contains none of the target HAP at or above the thresholds, verify whether any other lines at the facility spray-apply target HAP-containing coatings (to determine facility-wide applicability under Subpart HHHHHH).

If you are a motor vehicle/mobile equipment surface coating operation and claim no target HAP coatings, prepare and (if desired) submit the Administrator notification or petition described in 40 CFR 63.11170(a)(2) and retain the supporting records onsite for Administrator verification.

Determine annual volumes (liters or gallons) of coatings that contain HAP used at the facility and per operation to compare to the 946 L (250 gal) per year threshold and 189 L (50 gal) per coating exemption in 40 CFR 63.3881(c).

Determine whether the polyurea line or other coating activities qualify for any exclusions in §63.11169(d) (research/lab, quality control, facility maintenance) or in §63.3881(c)(2)-(17) (product-specific or process-specific exceptions).
Inventory whether the coatings, thinners, or cleaning materials used on the polyurea line contain organic HAP (per definitions in Subpart MMMM) to evaluate the §63.3881(c)(1) exemption.

Document which coating operations, storage/mixing vessels, and cleaning equipment are part of the affected source per 40 CFR 63.11171(b) and 40 CFR 63.3882(b) to determine whether the polyurea line is within an affected source boundary.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Combustion Turbines (Subpart YYYY)

criteria.criterion: If the stationary combustion turbine is located at a major source and is new or reconstructed (construction commenced after January 14, 2003), then it is an affected source subject to this subpart.

If the stationary combustion turbine is an existing unit (construction or reconstruction commenced on or before January 14, 2003), then it is not required to meet the requirements of this subpart and Subpart A for emission limitations and operating limitations.
If the unit is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine, then it must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart.

If the stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations to monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation (or petition for approval of no additional operating limitations) and must measure the specified parameters during the initial performance test and continuously thereafter.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations for a turbine without an oxidation catalyst, then your petition must include identification of the specific parameters to be limited, a discussion of the relationship between those parameters and HAP emissions, how you will set upper/lower values, the methods and instruments for measuring and monitoring including accuracy/precision, and the frequency and methods for recalibrating the instruments.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of no additional operating limitations for a turbine without an oxidation catalyst, then your petition must identify parameters that could change, discuss their relationship to HAP emissions, explain why limits are not possible, describe measurement and monitoring methods and recalibration, and explain why adopting parameters as limits is infeasible, unreasonable, or unnecessary.

If you are operating a stationary combustion turbine that must meet the formaldehyde emission limitation and you use an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor catalyst inlet temperature; if you are not using an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition.

If you are required to conduct performance tests, then you must follow the performance test requirements in Table 3 of this subpart, conduct three separate test runs each at least 1 hour, conduct tests at high load (100% ± 10%), and (for turbines without an oxidation catalyst) you must not conduct the initial performance test until after your petition has been approved or disapproved by the Administrator.

If you are required to submit notifications and performance-test-related notices, then you must submit the applicable Initial Notification, notification of intent to conduct an initial performance test at least 60 days before the test, and the Notification of Compliance Status (including performance test results) within 60 calendar days after completing the performance test.

If you are subject to the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must submit semiannual compliance reports per this subpart and keep records of notifications, performance tests, monitoring, deviations, and the records required in Table 5 to show continuous compliance.

If you are required to use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) after September 8, 2020, then you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures per § 63.8(d)(1)–(2) and keep those procedures on record.

If your unit is new or reconstructed and is a lean premix gas-fired turbine that started up after March 9, 2022, then it must comply with the emissions and operating limitations upon startup; if it started up on or before March 9, 2022, then it must comply no later than March 9, 2022.

If you must comply with emission and operating limitations, then at all times you must operate and maintain the turbine, any air pollution control equipment, and monitoring equipment in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAPs (subject status).
Confirm turbine construction/reconstruction commencement date to determine new vs existing (before or after Jan 14, 2003).
Confirm turbine startup date to determine applicable compliance date (before/on or after Mar 9, 2022).
Confirm turbine type: that it is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine as defined by the subpart.
Confirm whether the turbine is equipped with an oxidation catalyst (yes/no).

If no catalyst, prepare a petition to the Administrator and verify the petition will include: the specific parameters proposed for monitoring (e.g., turbine speed and inlet air temperature), the relationship between those parameters and HAP (formaldehyde) emissions, how upper/lower limits will be set, measurement and monitoring methods and instruments with accuracy/precision, and the recalibration frequency and methods (per 63.6120(f)).

If proposing no additional operating limitations, prepare a petition addressing identification of parameters that could change, relationship to HAPs, why limits cannot be established, measurement/monitoring methods and recalibration, and why limits are infeasible/unnecessary (per 63.6120(g)).

Do not conduct the initial performance test until after the Administrator approves or disapproves the petition (if the turbine has no oxidation catalyst) and schedule the notification of intent to test at least 60 days before the initial performance test.
Verify capability to continuously monitor the petition-specified parameters (and implement CMS quality control program and written procedures if a CMS is required after Sept 8, 2020).
Document and retain the chosen monitoring methods and instrument specifications (accuracy/precision) and a calibration schedule consistent with the petition.

Plan to perform performance tests per Table 3: three separate runs, each at least 1 hour, at high load (100% ±10%), and record process information demonstrating representativeness for the test period.

Prepare to submit Initial Notification, Notification of Compliance Status (including performance test results) within required timeframes, and to report via CEDRI/ERT as required for performance test reports.
Establish recordkeeping to retain notifications, performance test reports, monitoring data, deviations, calibration records, and the records required in Table 5 to show continuous compliance.

Verify whether any exceptions apply (e.g., unit is an emergency turbine, located on the North Slope of Alaska, rated peak power <1.0 MW, or burns ≥10% landfill/digester gas or gasified MSW) that would alter applicability or monitoring/reporting requirements (per 63.6090).

If proposing turbine speed and inlet air temperature as the monitored parameters, assemble data or justification showing how changes in those parameters affect formaldehyde emissions and how limits on them will ensure compliance (to include with the petition).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants From Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units (MATS)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in 40 CFR 63.10042, then this subpart applies to the unit.

If the unit burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input in any one of those calendar years, then the unit meets the definition of an oil-fired EGU and is subject to this subpart.
If the unit is an electric steam generating unit that is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU and meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.

If the unit is capable of combusting more than 25 MW of coal or oil but did not fire sufficient coal or oil to satisfy the average annual heat input requirement in §63.10042, then the unit is not subject to this subpart (even if capable of burning those fuels).

If the unit qualifies as a limited-use liquid oil-fired EGU (annual capacity factor when burning oil of less than 8 percent of its maximum or nameplate heat input averaged over a contiguous 24-month block), then it is a limited-use liquid oil-fired subcategory and is not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 (but remains subject to specified work practices).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (Major-source Boiler MACT)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to that boiler or process heater (except as excluded in §63.7491).
If the unit is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.
If the unit is a natural gas-fired EGU (as defined in subpart UUUUU) that fires at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.
If the boiler or process heater is not located at or is not part of a major source of HAP, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Is the unit an electric steam generating unit that produces electricity for sale (i.e., does it meet the EGU definition)? (see 40 CFR 63.10042)
What is the unit's maximum/net electric output (MWe) and is it capable of producing more than 25 MWe from combustion of fossil fuels? (see 40 CFR 63.10042 and 40 CFR 63.9983(c))
Which fuels are authorized in the operating permit and are the required fuel-handling facilities present (i.e., is the unit 'capable of combusting' coal or oil)? (see 40 CFR 63.10042)

Calculate the unit's heat-input fraction from oil: percentage of annual heat input from oil for each of the last 3 calendar years and the 3-year average; does it exceed 10% (3-year average) or 15% (any single year)? (see 40 CFR 63.10042)

If oil use is very low, calculate annual capacity factor when burning oil (is oil capacity factor <8% averaged over a contiguous 24-month block) to determine limited-use liquid oil-fired status. (see 40 CFR 63.10042 and 40 CFR 63.10011(c)(2)(iv))

If the unit burns predominantly natural gas, compute the annual fraction of heat input from natural gas (is it a natural gas-fired EGU and does it fire ≥85% natural gas if considering exclusion under DDDDD?). (see 40 CFR 63.10042 and 40 CFR 63.7491(a))
Is the facility a major source of HAP (determine whether facility-wide HAP emissions meet/exceed the major-source thresholds in §63.2)? (see 40 CFR 63.7485 and 40 CFR 63.7490)

If the unit is capable of burning coal or oil but has not actually fired sufficient coal/oil, document fuel usage records and permit/physical capability to confirm whether the unit meets the fuel-share thresholds in §63.10042. (see 40 CFR 63.9983(c) and 40 CFR 63.10042)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Area Source Standards for Glass Manufacturing (Subpart SSSSSS)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a glass manufacturing facility that manufactures flat glass, glass containers, or pressed and blown glass by melting a mixture of raw materials to produce molten glass and form the molten glass into shapes, is an area source of HAPs, and uses one or more continuous furnaces charged with compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP, then the facility is subject to subpart SSSSSS.

If a glass melting furnace is a continuous furnace, is charged with compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials, and is used to produce glass that contains one or more of the glass manufacturing metal HAP at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy), then that furnace is an affected furnace under this subpart.
If the furnace is a research and development process unit, then it is not an affected furnace under this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Paints and Allied Products Manufacturing Area Sources (Subpart CCCCCCC)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source of HAP emissions and processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP, then the facility is subject to subpart CCCCCCC.

If the operation produces materials intended to leave a dried film of solid material on a substrate (paints and allied products) and is of the type typically described by NAICS codes 3255 or 3259 produced by physical means such as blending and mixing, then the operation falls within the definition of paints and allied products manufacturing for this subpart.

If the operation is the manufacture of raw materials such as resins, pigments, and solvents used in the production of paints and coatings, then the operation is not included within paints and allied products manufacturing for this subpart.
If the facility no longer processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP and does not plan to do so in the future, then the facility is no longer subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Chemical Preparations Area Sources (Subpart BBBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical preparations facility (as defined in §63.11588) that is a stationary area source of HAP and has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service, then the facility is subject to subpart BBBBBBB.

If the chemical preparations operations at your facility are subject to the requirements specified in subpart VVVVVV or subpart CCCCCCC of this part, then the facility's chemical preparations operations are exempt from subpart BBBBBBB.

If a material (raw material, intermediate, or product) contains compounds of nickel in amounts greater than or equal to 0.1 percent by weight (as the metal) then that material is target HAP-containing and a chemical preparations operation that contains, contacts, or processes it is in target HAP service for purposes of this subpart.

If your operation is a 'chemical preparation' operation described by NAICS code 325998 (manufacture of target HAP-containing products or intermediates), then the chemical preparations definitions and requirements apply.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (Subpart VVVVVV)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source of HAP emissions and the CMPU uses as feedstock or generates as byproduct any Table 1 HAP present at the CMPU above the thresholds specified (e.g., quinoline, manganese, and/or trivalent chromium at >1.0 percent by weight or any other Table 1 HAP at >0.1 percent by weight), then the CMPU is subject to subpart VVVVVV.

If the unit of interest is part of a CMPU as defined for NAICS code 325 (i.e., it includes all process vessels, equipment, and activities necessary to operate a chemical manufacturing process that produces a material or family of materials described by NAICS 325), then the CMPU definition and associated applicability tests apply.

If the operations are within the manufacture of Paint and Allied Products subject to subpart CCCCCCC (or any other specifically listed chemical manufacturing area source category listed in §63.11494(c)(1)), then subpart VVVVVV does not apply to those operations.
If the operations are research and development facilities or other categories listed in §63.11494(c)(3)–(6), then those operations are not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Confirm the facility NAICS code(s) (e.g., 3255 for glass frit, 325998 for chemical preparations) for each production line or operation.
Determine whether frit production involves melting raw materials to produce molten glass and forming the molten glass (i.e., is it a glass manufacturing operation as defined in 40 CFR 63.11448(a)).
Verify whether the furnace(s) used for frit production are continuous furnaces (definition referenced in 40 CFR 63.11449(a)(1)) or are research and development units (40 CFR 63.11449(b)).
Confirm whether the furnace feedstock contains compounds of glass-manufacturing metal HAPs (including nickel) and at what concentration (see 40 CFR 63.11448(c) and 63.11449(a)(2)).
Calculate annual production rate of glass (or glass that contains metal HAP) from each furnace to verify whether it is at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) (40 CFR 63.11449(a)(3)).
Determine the facility's potential to emit (PTE) for individual HAPs and for total HAP to verify area-source status (below 10 tpy single HAP and below 25 tpy total HAP) per 40 CFR 63.11448(b).

Decide whether the frit product is a finished paint/coating (intended to leave a dried film on a substrate) or a raw material used in coatings/glazes, and document the intended use (40 CFR 63.11607 and 40 CFR 63.11599(a)).

If claiming the paints-and-allied-products exemption, document that the operation manufactures raw materials (e.g., frit) used in production of coatings rather than paints that leave a dried film (40 CFR 63.11607(3)).

If considering chemical preparations applicability, verify whether the operation is described by NAICS 325998 and whether chemical preparations equipment (mixing, blending, milling, extruding) is used to make target HAP-containing products (40 CFR 63.11579(a) and 63.11588).

Assess whether raw materials or intermediates contain nickel (or other target HAPs) at or above target thresholds (nickel compounds ≥0.1% by weight as metal) to determine 'target HAP service' for chemical preparations (40 CFR 63.11588).

For potential applicability to subpart VVVVVV, inventory CMPU feedstocks and byproducts for Table 1 HAPs and determine concentrations against the thresholds (e.g., manganese or Cr(III) >1.0% or other Table 1 HAP >0.1%) (40 CFR 63.11494(a)(2)).

Confirm whether the frit/manufacturing operations are already subject to subpart CCCCCCC (paints) or subpart BBBBBBB (chemical preparations), because those make subpart VVVVVV inapplicable to those operations (40 CFR 63.11494(c)(1)(i); 40 CFR 63.11579(f)).
Document whether any control devices are federally enforceable and necessary to keep the source at area-source levels (which can affect permitting obligations under 40 CFR 63.11494(e)).

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing Operations (Coatings NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations that are located at or are part of a major source of HAP emissions, then the source may be subject to this subpart.

If you manufacture a material that meets the definition of 'coating' (produced by a manufacturing operation where materials are blended, mixed, diluted, or otherwise formulated), then the operation may be subject to this subpart.
If your operations process, use, or produce HAP, then the operations may be subject to this subpart.
If the equipment or operations are part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63, then those operations are not subject to this subpart.

If a formulation component is synthesized by chemical reaction or separation activity and then transferred to another vessel where it is formulated (i.e., the component is produced by synthesis/separation prior to formulation), then that material is not a 'coating' for purposes of this subpart.

If equipment used for both miscellaneous coating manufacturing and as part of a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process unit (MCPU) meets the conditions in § 63.8090(c)(1)–(5) (process unit group primary product = organic chemicals, records, and deadlines), then compliance with subpart FFFF may be deemed to satisfy this subpart for that equipment.

If the operation is an affiliated operation located at an affected source under the listed surface-coating subparts (e.g., subparts GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, SSSS), then the miscellaneous coating manufacturing requirements of this subpart do not apply to those affiliated operations.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (MCPU NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) located at or part of a major source of HAP emissions, then the MCPU may be subject to this subpart.

If the process unit produces materials described in § 63.2435(b)(1) (organic chemicals classified under the cited SIC/NAICS codes, certain quaternary ammonium compounds, hydrazine, or solvent recovery activities), then the unit may be an MCPU subject to this subpart.
If the MCPU processes, uses, or generates any organic HAP listed in CAA section 112(b) or hydrogen halide and halogen HAP, then the unit may be subject to this subpart.

If the MCPU consists of equipment used collectively to perform reaction, recovery, separation, purification, or other activities to produce a product or isolated intermediate (including filtration as a unit operation), then filtration/separation used to produce or purify chemical products is part of an MCPU and may make the unit subject to this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.2550 (definition of miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process and unit operation)

criteria.criterion: If the MCPU is part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 (i.e., is an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart), then it is not subject to this subpart except as specified in § 63.2435(b)(3).

If the operations at the facility are 'affiliated operations' located at an affected source under certain listed surface-coating subparts (GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, SSSS), then those affiliated operations are excluded from this subpart.

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing (Subpart VVVVVV definitions and applicability elements)

criteria.criterion: If your operation is a chemical manufacturing process (CMPU) that collectively functions to produce a product or isolated intermediate (including any separation or filtration steps used to separate or purify products), then the CMPU definitions in this subpart apply.

If you have batch process vents, including vents on filters or centrifuges that are part of a CMPU, then those vents meet the definition of batch process vents for applicability under chemical manufacturing provisions.
If the CMPU processes or emits wastewater or HAP that meet the wastewater definitions in this subpart, then the wastewater provisions in this subpart apply.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products (Plastic Parts Coating NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate surface coating of plastic parts or products (coating application to a substrate, including associated activities directly related to application) and you use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP and the facility is a major source (or located at a major source), then this subpart applies.

If the operation is not surface coating (for example, formulation, blending, or filtering of a coating product for sale or distribution rather than applying coating to a substrate), then the surface-coating subpart does not apply to that non-application activity.

If the coating operation meets any exclusion in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(17) (for example the facility uses only materials that contain no organic HAP or the activity falls under another specified NESHAP subpart), then this subpart does not apply.

checklist: Is the facility (or the affected source that includes the process) a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP)? (see 40 CFR 63.7985(a)(1), 63.2435(a), 63.4481(b))

Is the product you manufacture a 'coating' as defined in 40 CFR 63.8105 (i.e., produced by blending, mixing, diluting, or otherwise formulating for application to a substrate) or is it a formulation component produced earlier by synthesis or separation and then transferred for later formulation? (see 40 CFR 63.8105(c) and 63.8105 (Coating definition))
Does the process 'process, use, or produce' HAP (identify which HAP and estimated quantities emitted/consumed)? (see 40 CFR 63.7985(a)(3), 63.2435(b)(2))

Is the final filtering step a separation/purification activity performed to remove solids/lumps/gels as part of producing or purifying a chemical product (i.e., is filtration used as a unit operation to produce the product or an isolated intermediate) or is it simply a final quality-control step within a coating formulation intended for application? (see 40 CFR 63.2550 (unit operation/process) and 40 CFR 63.8105(c))

Are the pieces of equipment used (filters, centrifuges, process vessels) part of a collective process that would meet the MCPU/CMPU definitions (reaction, recovery, separation, purification) and fall under NAICS/SIC classifications cited in §63.2435(b)(1)? (see 40 CFR 63.2435(b)(1), 63.2550, 63.11502)

Do you use ≥378 L (100 gal)/yr of coatings that contain HAP in operations that apply coatings to plastic substrates (i.e., surface coating activity), and is the coating actually applied to a substrate on-site? (see 40 CFR 63.4481(a)(1), (b))

Is any of the equipment/operations already part of an affected source under another NESHAP subpart (including subpart FFFF) or otherwise assigned to another subpart—if yes, identify which and review the cross-subpart assignment rules (process unit groups, affiliated operations)? (see 40 CFR 63.7985(a)(4), 63.8090(c), 63.2435(c)(3))

What are the sizes/capacities of process vessels (e.g., ≥250 gal process vessels per coating subpart definition) and throughputs (annual coating usage, HAP consumption) to determine thresholds? (see 40 CFR 63.8105 (process vessel) and 40 CFR 63.2550 (process vessel/storage tank thresholds))

Does the operation generate process vents, batch process vents, or wastewater streams (identify vents/points of determination and estimate HAP concentrations/flows) that would trigger Group 1/Group 2 classifications under subpart FFFF or FFFF-related provisions? (see 40 CFR 63.2550 (wastewater/point of determination), 63.2460(b))

If you have mixed use equipment (coating operations plus chemical manufacturing), can you form a process unit group (PUG) and identify the primary product according to § 63.2535(l) and the record/documentation requirements in § 63.8090(c)? (see 40 CFR 63.8090(c)(1)–(5))

candidates.title: Petroleum Refinery NESHAP (Subpart CC)

criteria.criterion: If the combustion device lacks an enclosed combustion chamber and uses an uncontrolled volume of ambient air to burn gases, then the device is a flare and is subject to the Subpart CC flare requirements in §63.670.

If the combustion device is an enclosed combustion device used for destroying organic compounds (an incinerator) or is an enclosed combustion device that extracts useful energy in the form of steam (a boiler or process heater), then it is not a flare and would be treated as an incinerator/boiler/process heater for purposes of control and monitoring (e.g., the monitoring requirements in §63.644 for miscellaneous process vents using such devices).

If the control of a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent is achieved by a flare, then on and after January 30, 2019 the flare must meet the requirements of §63.670; if the Group 1 vent is controlled by a non-flare control device the device must meet the 98 weight-percent or 20 ppmv limit in §63.643(a)(2) and the applicable monitoring provisions in §63.644.

If the vapors are routed to a fuel gas system (rather than directly to an open combustor), then vents routed to the fuel gas system are not miscellaneous process vents under §63.641(3) and any flares receiving gas from the fuel gas system are subject to §63.670 on and after January 30, 2019.
citations: 40 CFR 63.641 (closed vent system / fuel gas system definitions)

checklist: Is the vapor combustor physically enclosed (i.e., does it have an enclosed combustion chamber) or is it an open tip/stack that entrains uncontrolled ambient air?

Does the combustor's manufacturer/design and operation extract useful energy (steam or useful heat) (i.e., boiler/process heater) or is it described as an incinerator (destroying organics) in design documentation?
Does the device rely on assist air/steam or uncontrolled ambient air at the tip (design drawings/specs showing flare-tip geometry, assist systems, or absence of enclosure)?
Is the unit installed/operated as part of a flare/header system (connected to flare header, multiple burners, water seal, pilot) or as a standalone enclosed combustor with a defined firebox/stack?
Are the vapors from the Plant 2 loading rack routed directly to the combustor or first routed into the refinery fuel gas system (pipe diagrams, P&IDs, and valve/line routing)?
Does the vent stream meet the Subpart CC definition of a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent (TOC ≥ 20 ppmv and VOC emission thresholds) so that §§63.643/63.644 could apply?
Is the plant site a major source as defined by CAA section 112(a) (to confirm Subpart CC applicability) and is the loading rack located within the affected source as defined in §63.640?

If the device appears to be a flare, determine whether it is pressure-assisted, air- or steam-assisted, its smokeless design capacity, pilot system, and whether it is subject to the specific monitoring/CPMS requirements in §63.670/63.671 (equipment specs, pilot configuration, flow/composition monitoring capability).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Paper and Other Web Coating Operations

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a major source of HAP and operates one or more web coating lines (as defined), then the facility is subject to Subpart JJJJ.

If a coating operation does not coat a continuous flexible substrate (a web that can be wound or unwound) and therefore is not a 'web coating line' as defined, then that operation is not subject to Subpart JJJJ as a web coating line.

If a web coating line at the facility is covered by one of the specific exclusions (e.g., included in subpart KK, subpart EE, subpart SSSS, subpart OOOO, or is research/laboratory equipment), then that line is not part of the affected source for Subpart JJJJ.

If a web coating line coats both paper/other web substrates and another substrate, then the subpart that applies is determined by the predominant activity (≥90 percent of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period), and Subpart JJJJ applies only if the web/paper activity is predominant.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Refractory Products Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a refractory products manufacturing facility (a plant site that manufactures refractory products as defined) and the plant site is a major source of HAP, then the facility is subject to Subpart SSSSS.

If the finished product meets the definition of a 'refractory product' (nonmetallic, <50 percent carbon by weight, and having properties that make it applicable for structures exposed to temperatures above 538 °C (1000 °F)), then that product is a refractory product for purposes of Subpart SSSSS.

If the mica insulation product does not meet the refractory-product definition (for example, it is not intended for or suitable for high-temperature lining/service above 538 °C and does not have the requisite refractory material properties), then manufacture of that product is not a refractory products manufacturing facility for Subpart SSSSS purposes.

If refractory products manufactured at the facility are resin-bonded, pitch-bonded, or otherwise use substances that are organic HAPs (i.e., the products or process contain or release organic HAP), then those refractory-product operations are the kinds of refractory products and processes addressed by Subpart SSSSS.

checklist: Confirm whether the plant is a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 10 tons/year or combined HAP ≥ 25 tons/year) per 40 CFR 63.9782(b).

For each production line, verify whether the substrate is a 'web' (continuous, flexible substrate able to be wound/unwound) and whether coating stations apply a continuous layer across the web width to determine if each line meets the 'web coating line' definition (40 CFR 63.3310).
For the roll-fed mica line: document whether mica paper is fed as a continuous web from unwind to rewind and whether coating is applied continuously across the web (to test web-coating status).

For the sheet-handled mica line: document whether material is processed as discrete sheets (not wound/unwound) and whether coating is applied in a continuous layer on a flexible web (to determine non-web status).

Determine whether any web coating line at the plant is excluded under 40 CFR 63.3300(a)–(g) (e.g., is it part of a printing/publishing press subject to subpart KK, magnetic tape operations, metal coil coating, textile coating under OOOO, or research/lab equipment).

If a line coats multiple substrate types, calculate the predominant activity (mass of substrate coated) over a representative period (at least one year where available) to see if ≥90% is paper/web per 40 CFR 63.3300(h).

If relying on Subpart JJJJ compliance options, inventory coatings used on web lines: obtain as-purchased and as-applied organic HAP content, volatile organic content, and coating solids (per 40 CFR 63.3360 and 63.3370) and monthly coating mass applied.

For refractory applicability, document the intended end-use and material properties of the finished mica insulation (does it function as a refractory lining or component exposed to temperatures >538 °C (1000 °F)?), and determine carbon content by weight to see if <50% carbon per 40 CFR 63.9824.

Document manufacturing steps for the mica product (e.g., crushing/grinding raw refractory raw materials, mixing with binders/additives, forming, drying, firing) to evaluate whether the plant is a 'refractory products manufacturing facility' per 40 CFR 63.9782(a) and 63.9824.

Identify whether binders, resins, pitches, or additives used in the mica product contain organic HAPs (and quantify potential to emit) since Subpart SSSSS targets refractory products that use organic HAPs (40 CFR 63.9824).

If uncertain about product classification, collect technical product specification sheets (composition, intended thermal service temperature, carbon content) and process flow descriptions to support the determination under 40 CFR 63.9824 and 40 CFR 63.9782.

candidates.title: Area Source Boilers NESHAP (Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers) (Subpart JJJJJJ)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler located at or part of an area source of hazardous air pollutants, then the boiler is subject to this subpart unless an exemption in § 63.11195 applies.

If a boiler meets the definition of a gas-fired boiler (i.e., burns gaseous fuels and burns liquid fuel only during periods of gas curtailment, supply interruption, startups, or periodic testing/maintenance/training with testing not exceeding 48 hours per calendar year), then the boiler is not subject to this subpart under the gas-fired boiler exemption.

If a boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) as defined in this subpart (fossil fuel-fired unit >25 MW serving a generator that produces electricity for sale, or a cogenerator meeting the stated thresholds), then the boiler (EGU) is not subject to this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.11237 (definition of Electric utility steam generating unit (EGU))

criteria.criterion: If a boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard under this part or under a section 129 standard or is otherwise listed in § 63.11195(a)–(d),(g)–(j), then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source of HAPs (i.e., does not meet the major source thresholds) and that the boilers are located at or part of that area source.
Confirm each boiler's classification: is it an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler under § 63.11237?

For each boiler, document fuel types actually burned and operating patterns: whether the unit burns only gaseous fuels (natural gas) except for limited liquid-fuel use during gas curtailment, supply interruption, startups, or maintenance/training, and whether combined periodic liquid-fuel testing/maintenance/training is ≤ 48 hours per calendar year (per the gas-fired boiler definition).

If the boilers produce electricity, determine if they meet the EGU definition: nameplate/electrical output >25 megawatts and serve a generator that produces electricity for sale, or cogenerate and supply >1/3 of potential electric output and >25 MW to any utility power distribution system; also verify whether the unit is 'capable of combusting' fossil fuels per the EGU definition (e.g., fuels allowed in permits and appropriate fuel handling facilities onsite).

Check whether the boilers are covered by any other NESHAP or section 129 standard, are subject to RCRA §3005 permitting, or are otherwise listed in § 63.11195(a)–(d),(g)–(k) (e.g., electric boilers, temporary, residential, seasonal, control-device boilers).

Review permits and permit conditions to see which fuels are authorized (to help assess EGU capability and the gas-fired boiler definition) and any federally enforceable limits (e.g., limited-use boiler annual capacity factor ≤ 10%).

Document historical fuel usage (monthly/annual) and any instances of burning non-gaseous fuels to support applicability determinations (including whether any liquid-fuel use exceeded the 48-hour testing/maintenance allowance).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at, or part of, a major source of HAP, then you are subject to this subpart.

If the boiler or process heater is part of the affected source that is subject to another subpart of this part (for example boilers/process heaters used as control devices to comply with subparts JJJ, OOO, PPP, and U), then it is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler or process heater is used as a control device to comply with another subpart of this part or parts 60, 61, or 65 and at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard, then it is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Boilers at Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If the boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard under this part, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.
If the boiler is a gas-fired boiler as defined in this subpart, then it is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler is used as a control device to comply with another subpart of this part or parts 60, 61, or 65 and at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard, then it is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility and the facility is located at a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to the affected source at that facility.
If a combustion unit exhaust stream is routinely used to direct-fire a PCWP dryer or lumber kiln, then that combustion unit (and its exhaust) is part of the affected source covered by this subpart.

If a combustion unit is used to directly-fire a PCWP dryer or lumber kiln, then you must conduct annual combustion-unit tune-ups and monitor usage of combustion-unit bypass stacks as required by this subpart.

If a process unit exhaust stream is allowed to temporarily vent to the atmosphere while bypassing a control device routinely used to meet the compliance options in tables 1B/1C/1D/1E, then you must install and operate a sensor to continuously monitor process-unit bypass stack usage.

If your process units (including dryers, refiners, and associated combustion exhaust streams) are included in the definition of the affected source for PCWP manufacturing, then you must meet the compliance options, operating requirements, and work practice requirements specified in this subpart for those process units.

checklist: Is your facility a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility (does it manufacture plywood, particleboard, fiberboard, oriented strandboard, or similar products)?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (>=10 t/yr of any single HAP or >=25 t/yr total HAP)?
Does any combustion unit or gasifier exhaust stream routinely direct-fire a PCWP dryer or lumber kiln (i.e., is the hot gas stream intentionally routed through the dryer as part of normal operation)?
Are the dryers that receive gasifier hot gas covered by Subpart DDDD (PCWP NESHAP) at your facility?

Is any portion of the gasifier/combustion exhaust intentionally bypassing the dryers (e.g., routed to heat thermal oil) via a bypass stack or other vent, and is that bypassed flow episodic or routine?
Is the gasification unit/combustion unit operated as a control device to comply with another NESHAP or subpart (and if so, which subpart)?

What fraction (percent) of the average annual heat input to the boiler/process heater comes from regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard (computed over any 3 consecutive calendar years)?
Is the boiler/process heater gas-fired (check the fuel type and how 'gas-fired' is defined in the applicable subpart)?
Is the unit specifically listed as an affected source in any other NESHAP or in a standard established under CAA section 129?

Do you have combustion-unit bypass stacks or process-unit bypass stacks, and do you have or plan to install continuous monitors (e.g., damper position, temperature) for bypass usage as described in this subpart?

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a PCWP manufacturing facility (a facility that manufactures plywood and/or composite wood products, and includes lumber kilns), then this subpart can apply to you.

If the PCWP manufacturing facility is located at a major source of HAP emissions (any single HAP ≥ 9.07 megagrams (10 tons)/yr or any combination of HAP ≥ 22.68 megagrams (25 tons)/yr), then this subpart applies to that facility.

If a collection of dryers, refiners, blenders, formers, presses, board coolers and other process units used in manufacturing plywood and composite wood products (including lumber kilns) exist at the facility, then those units are part of the affected source regulated by this subpart.

If you commenced construction of an affected source after January 9, 2003, then that affected source is a new affected source (subject to the new-source provisions if the applicability criteria were met at commencement).

If an area source increases its emissions or potential to emit such that it becomes a major source of HAP, then the facility must be in compliance with this subpart by October 1, 2007 or upon initial startup of the affected source as a major source, whichever is later.
If you operate lumber kilns at a facility subject to this subpart, then the work practice and O&M requirements specific to lumber kilns in this subpart apply to those kilns.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Part 63 General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: If a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit any hazardous air pollutant and is subject to any standard, limitation, prohibition, or other federally enforceable requirement established pursuant to part 63, then the provisions of this part (general provisions) apply to the owner or operator.

If an area source that would otherwise be subject to a part 63 standard becomes a major source (by increasing emissions or potential to emit), then the source is subject to the notification requirements of this subpart and may become subject to major-source requirements.

If an area source that previously was a major source becomes a major source again, then it is subject to the applicable major-source requirements under this part immediately upon becoming a major source again (provided the compliance date for the major-source requirements has passed).

If a stationary source's emissions or potential to emit equal or exceed 10 tons per year of any single HAP or 25 tons per year of combined HAP, then that stationary source meets the definition of a 'major source' under part 63.

checklist: Do you own or operate a plywood and/or composite wood products manufacturing facility as defined in 40 CFR 63.2292 (confirm product types and processes on site)?
Does your facility include lumber kilns (confirm number, type: batch/continuous, direct-fired/indirect-fired)?

What are your current actual and potential to emit annual HAP emissions (calculate for methanol and for total HAP); include consideration of enforceable limits and control equipment when calculating potential to emit?
Does any single HAP (e.g., methanol) equal or exceed 10 tons per year, or do combined HAP equal or exceed 25 tons per year (use the definitions and accounting methods in 40 CFR part 63)?
Is the facility part of a group of stationary sources within a contiguous area and under common control (confirm plant/site boundary and corporate/common-control arrangements)?
Is the source currently classified as an 'area source' or a 'major source' under part 63 today (document current classification and basis)?
If currently an area source, will the planned production increase raise actual emissions or potential to emit above the major-source thresholds (provide emissions projection calculations)?

If emissions will increase, when will that increase be effective (date emissions change or date a permit revision/reclassification becomes effective) and are there any enforceable permit limits that constrain potential to emit?
Have you commenced construction or reconstruction of any affected source components after January 9, 2003 (to determine 'new' affected source status)?

If you become subject to the subpart, have you identified the affected source equipment (dryers, refiners, blenders, presses, lumber kilns, etc.) and the compliance obligations (notifications, work practice/O&M, tune-ups, site-specific plans) and the relevant compliance dates in 40 CFR 63.2233 and related sections?

If you plan to use a site-specific plan option for lumber kilns, are you aware of the site-specific plan submission and approval timing and title V incorporation requirements (e.g., submission deadlines and permit reopening requirements)?
Confirm whether any existing federally enforceable permit limits currently restrict your potential to emit (identify permit provisions that could affect major-source determination).

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source and Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU above the concentration thresholds specified in § 63.11494(a)(2)(i)-(iv), then the CMPU is subject to this subpart.

If the CMPU is comprised as described in § 63.11494(b) (i.e., process vessels, equipment, activities, and associated storage/transfer/surge/bottoms receivers for NAICS 325 materials), then those units are included in the affected source determination for this subpart.

If your operations or products fall within any of the exemptions listed in § 63.11494(c)(1)-(6) or the excluded NAICS/product items in § 63.11494(c)(2), then those operations are not subject to this subpart.

If an area source has installed a federally-enforceable control device on an affected CMPU and that control device is necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area-source levels, then the area source is required to obtain a title V permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 71 as a result of this subpart.

If you are a new or existing affected source as defined in § 63.11494(d) (facility-wide collection of CMPUs and associated heat exchange and wastewater systems meeting (a) and (b)), then this subpart's requirements apply to the affected source as indicated in § 63.11494(d).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit any HAP and is subject to any standard, limitation, prohibition, or other federally enforceable requirement established under part 63, then the owner or operator must comply with the provisions of that standard and with subpart A as provided in § 63.1(b)(1).

If an area-source standard explicitly gives States the option to exclude area sources affected by that standard from the title V requirement, then States may exclude those area sources from the obligation to obtain a title V permit under § 63.1(b)(2)(i).

If a relevant area-source standard fails to specify what the permitting requirements will be for area sources affected by that standard, then area sources subject to the standard will be subject to the requirement to obtain a title V permit under § 63.1(b)(2)(iii).

If a source's potential to emit, considering physical or operational limitations (including controls) that are federally enforceable, is below the major-source thresholds, then the source is an area source and not a major source under the definition in § 63.2.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility contains one or more chemical manufacturing process units (CMPUs) as defined in § 63.11494(b).

Determine whether the facility is an area source (PTE below major-source thresholds) or a major source, and document potential to emit both with and without any physical or operational limitations/controls (see definition of Major source in 40 CFR 63.2).

For each CMPU, verify presence and concentrations of Table 1 HAP in feedstocks, byproducts, process/waste streams, or products against the thresholds in § 63.11494(a)(2)(i)-(iv) (use SDS/formulation data or engineering assessment as allowed).

Verify whether any operations or products at the facility fall under the exemptions in § 63.11494(c)(1)-(6) or § 63.11494(c)(2) (e.g., paints/allied products, specific NAICS exclusions, R&D labs, QA/QC labs, ancillary activities).

If you have federally enforceable limits established prior to this rule, confirm those limits are in a federally enforceable mechanism (e.g., title V permit condition, SIP, federal permit, consent agreement) consistent with the definition of federally enforceable in § 63.2.

Identify any control devices on affected CMPUs and determine whether those control devices are federally enforceable and whether they are necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area-source levels (i.e., without the control the source would be a major source) per § 63.11494(e).

If controls are federally enforceable and necessary to stay an area source, verify title V permit obligations and applicable deadlines in § 63.11494(e) and consult the applicable permitting authority (part 70/71) for submission dates.

Check whether any other subpart provided (e.g., chemical preparations, paints, boilers, hazardous waste combustors) covers any part of your operations, since those subparts may exempt or change title V applicability (see cross-references in the relevant subparts and § 63.11494(c)).

Confirm State/title V permitting program policy: whether the State has opted to exclude area sources for this specific standard per § 63.1(b)(2)(i) or otherwise applies the permit requirement (contact permitting authority).

candidates.title: Municipal Solid Waste Landfills (Subpart AAAA)

criteria.criterion: If the landfill accepted waste since November 8, 1987 (or has additional capacity for waste deposition) and is a major source, collocated with a major source, or is an area source with design capacity ≥ 2.5 million Mg and uncontrolled NMOC emissions ≥ 50 Mg/yr, then the landfill is subject to this subpart.

If the landfill includes a bioreactor and accepts waste since November 8, 1987 and is a major source, collocated with a major source, or is an area source with design capacity ≥ 2.5 million Mg and 2.5 million m3 (and is not permanently closed as of Jan 16, 2003), then the landfill is subject to this subpart.
If the landfill meets the criteria in §63.1935, then the entire MSW landfill (the contiguous disposal facility) is the affected source under this subpart.

If you plan to cap, remove, or decommission the gas collection and control system, then the landfill must be closed, the collection and control system must have been in operation a minimum of 15 years or you must demonstrate the system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow, and the calculated NMOC emission rate must be < 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates (each 90–180 days apart), then the collection and control system may be removed.

If you intend to remove or cease operation of the control equipment, then you must submit an equipment removal report to the Administrator at least 30 days prior that includes a closure report, either the initial performance test report demonstrating the 15-year minimum control period has expired or information demonstrating inability to operate 15 years due to declining flows, and dated copies of three successive NMOC emission rate reports.

If you are decommissioning an individual well (not the entire collection/control system), then a decommissioned well may experience static positive pressure after shutdown but design changes (including removing wells) must be approved by the Administrator as specified in the design-plan/approval provisions.

If you must calculate NMOC emission rate after installation/startup for purposes of determining system removal, then use the flow-measurement at the common header pipe and NMOC concentration from the common header pipe (sampled before any gas-moving or condensate removal equipment) per the procedures in §63.1959(c) to determine MNMOC for the capping/removal test.

checklist: Verify whether the landfill accepted waste on or after November 8, 1987 or has additional capacity for waste deposition.
Confirm whether the landfill is a major source or is collocated with a major source (per 40 CFR 63.2 definitions).

Confirm the landfill design capacity from the most recent state/local/tribal permit and include in-place waste to verify whether design capacity ≥ 2.5 million Mg (document calculations and site-specific density if converting units).
Determine whether the landfill includes a bioreactor as defined in §63.1990.

Verify whether the landfill is closed (no additional waste will be placed without filing a notification of modification) and whether a closure report has been or will be submitted to the Administrator.
