Establish whether the action is removal/decommissioning of the entire gas collection and control system or only an individual well (EW-308A); document the scope of removal.

Document the installation and start-up dates and total continuous operation time of the collection and control system and of well EW-308A (installed May 2018) to compare to the 15‑year minimum operation requirement.

If claiming inability to operate 15 years due to declining gas flow, assemble the evidence or performance test data demonstrating declining flows (per §63.1981(g)(1)(ii)) and be prepared to include that in the equipment removal report.

Obtain three successive NMOC emission rate determinations showing MNMOC < 50 Mg/yr, with each test date at least 90 days apart and no more than 180 days apart, using the procedures in §63.1959 (including header flow measurement and header NMOC sampling where applicable). Record test dates and methods.

If using header measurements for NMOC, ensure sampling is performed on the common header pipe before any gas-moving or condensate removal equipment and flow is measured with a device calibrated per EPA Method 2E as required in §63.1959(c).

Prepare the equipment removal report at least 30 days prior to removal including: closure report, performance test report or documentation showing inability to operate 15 years, and dated copies (or CDX submission statements and dates) of the three successive NMOC emission rate reports per §63.1981(g).

If removing only a well, determine whether design-plan amendments or Administrator approval are required for the design change and prepare to submit revised design plan information as specified in §63.1981(d).

Confirm required monitoring and recordkeeping (e.g., wellhead pressure, temperature, gas composition) are current and available to support any root cause or corrective action analyses if positive pressure or temperature issues arise during decommissioning per §§63.1960–63.1961 and §63.1981(h).
Plan report submission route and timing: electronic reporting via CEDRI/CDX where required (see §63.1981(l)) and allow Administrator review time for design-plan approvals or removal notifications.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) (Subpart DDDD)

criteria.criterion: If you elect a production-based compliance option then you must meet that production-based total HAP compliance option for that specific process unit and you need only meet one compliance option for each process unit (you may not mix production-based and add-on control options for the same process unit).

If equipment is a reconstituted wood product press or a reconstituted wood product board cooler then that equipment is a process unit and must be evaluated under the compliance options and operating requirements that apply to process units.

If you choose a concentration-based compliance option for an add-on control system outlet for a reconstituted wood product press (new or existing) or for a reconstituted wood product board cooler at a new affected source then the capture device for that press or board cooler must be a wood products enclosure as defined in §63.2292 or must achieve a capture efficiency ≥ 95 percent.

If you use a production-based compliance option then you must measure and record the process-unit throughput during each performance test and calculate mass per unit production for that process unit using Equation 2 (which incorporates capture efficiency for presses and board coolers), applying the nondetect data treatment rules in §63.2262(g).

If you use an add-on control system that collects emissions from one or more process units then you must calculate percent reduction across the control system using capture efficiency and inlet/outlet emission rates according to Equation 1 to determine whether the control-system-based compliance option is met.

If you must demonstrate initial compliance for a press or board cooler then you must conduct performance tests under representative operating conditions with the required number and duration of runs, collect the required monitoring and production data, document capture efficiency (for presses/board coolers) using Methods 204/204A–204F or the alternative tracer gas method, and submit the results with your Notification of Compliance Status.

If a single control device is used to control a combination of equipment including a reconstituted wood product press or board cooler then routine control device maintenance exemption limits (maximum percent of annual operating uptime) apply per process unit category and may differ (e.g., 0.5% for presses/board coolers unless combined with equipment in the 3% category).

checklist: Confirm that the press and board cooler meet the Subpart DDDD definitions of 'reconstituted wood product press' and 'reconstituted wood product board cooler' (§63.2292).

Determine whether each press and board cooler is at a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source and note construction/start dates (check applicability/compliance dates in §63.2232 and §63.2233).

Decide and document which compliance option (production-based per Table 1A or add-on control per Table 1B/1C/1D/1E) you intend to use for each individual process unit (press and board cooler) — one option per process unit. (See §63.2240.)

If choosing production-based options, record the process-unit throughput (P) for each unit and ensure performance tests measure ER for that unit and apply Equation 2 for mass per unit production (include capture efficiency for press/board cooler). (See §63.2262(f),(i).)

If choosing add-on concentration-based options for a press or a new board cooler, verify the capture device is a wood products enclosure meeting the design criteria or obtain a measured capture efficiency ≥95% (Methods 204/204A–204F or alternative tracer gas) and retain enclosure design documentation or capture-efficiency test reports. (See §63.2240(b), §63.2267, §63.2292.)

If emissions from the press and board cooler are routed to the same control device, determine inlet and outlet emission rates and capture efficiency and calculate percent reduction across the control system using Equation 1 to evaluate compliance for the control sequence. (See §63.2262(h).)

Collect and retain performance-test records conducted under representative operating conditions (three runs of required duration), 15-minute monitoring during tests, nondetect handling, and any site-specific operating limits established by tests; prepare Notification of Compliance Status with these results. (See §63.2262(b),(c),(e),(g) and §63.2260(c).)

If a control device serves multiple process units, document planned routine maintenance and verify applicable maintenance-exemption uptime limits by equipment category (e.g., 0.5% vs. 3%) and ensure any approved exemption is incorporated into Title V permit as required. (See §63.2251(b)–(d).)

Determine whether any process streams are 'mixed PCWP process streams' (co-mingled with streams subject to earlier compliance options) which may affect applicable compliance option timelines and requirements. (See §63.2292 and §63.2240(d)(5).)

Confirm submission deadlines and compliance dates applicable to your source (initial startup dates, July 6, 2026/2029 phased requirements) and plan testing/notifications accordingly. (See §63.2233 and §63.2240(d).)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Rubber Tire Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.
If the facility is not located at or part of a major source of HAP emissions (i.e., is an area source and does not meet the major-source thresholds), then you are not subject to this subpart.

If your operations at a rubber tire manufacturing facility include an affected source composed of tire production processes that use or process cements and solvents (including tire repair operations, tire building, tread and cement operations, undertread cement operations, green tire spray, bead cementing, slab dip, etc.), then those processes are tire production affected sources covered by this subpart when the facility meets the major-source criterion.

If your affected source is limited to tire cord production but the primary product produced at that affected source is determined to be subject to another subpart as of the effective date of that subpart or startup, then that affected source is not subject to this subpart.

If your affected source is a research and development facility whose primary purpose is R&D into new processes and products, operated under close supervision of technically trained personnel and not engaged in manufacture of products for commercial sale (except de minimis), then the affected source is not subject to this subpart.

If the processes in question do not use cements and solvents as defined in this subpart, then those processes are not part of the tire production affected source and are not subject to the tire production emission limits of this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is located at or is part of a major source of HAPs (calculate potential to emit including controls: any single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or total HAPs ≥ 25 tpy).

Inventory all on-site activities to confirm whether you perform rubber tire manufacturing or components production vs only retreading/repair, and list which operations are performed (e.g., tire building, repair, tread/cement operations, bead cementing, green tire spray, slab dip, extruding where solvents/cements used).
Verify whether your tire retreading/repair operations use or process cements and solvents (as defined in the subpart) and identify each cement/solvent product used.
For each cement/solvent used, obtain HAP mass-percent information (MSDS/CPDS/manufacturer data or perform EPA Method 311) to support applicability and compliance calculations.

If you only perform tire cord production, determine the primary product for the affected source and whether that product is subject to another NESHAP subpart as of the other subpart’s effective date/startup.
Determine whether the facility is an R&D facility (primary purpose R&D, close supervision by trained personnel, not engaged in commercial manufacture except de minimis).

If planning to claim emission reductions from add-on control devices, document the control device type and planned monitoring parameters and whether you will route affected process streams to the control device.
Quantify monthly and annual rubber used (megagrams) and monthly mass of each cement/solvent used to support production-based or HAP-constituent compliance demonstrations if subject.

candidates.title: Petroleum Refinery Catalytic Cracking Units (NESHAP Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: if the process vent is a catalyst regeneration flue gas vent on a fluid catalytic cracking unit at a petroleum refinery then the source is an affected source under this subpart

if the catalytic cracking unit does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (i.e., complete combustion units with no additional combustion devices) then you may use the alternative volumetric flow-rate procedure in 40 CFR 63.1573(a)(1) (air flow + temperature correction) instead of direct stack flow measurement (e.g., Method 2) to determine regenerator exhaust gas flow rate

if you have a gas analyzer installed in the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust vent prior to the addition of air or other gas streams and you continuously measure and record Qa and CO2, CO, and O2 concentrations then you may use the alternative calculation in 40 CFR 63.1573(a)(2) to determine Qr (the volumetric flow rate of exhaust gas before adding air or gas streams)

if you elect Option 1b (NSPS coke burn-off limit) or Option 2 (PM per coke burn-off) to demonstrate PM compliance then you must compute PM emission rate using the coke burn-off and flow equations in 40 CFR 63.1564 (Equations 1–3) and you may use the alternative procedures in 40 CFR 63.1573(a)(1) or (2) as applicable to calculate Qr for those equations

checklist: Confirm the unit is a fluid catalytic cracking unit at a petroleum refinery (affected source per 40 CFR 63.1562(b)(1)).

Determine whether any other gas streams (e.g., oxygen-enriched air, nitrogen, recycle gases) are introduced into the catalyst regeneration vent prior to the sampling point (if none, §63.1573(a)(1) may apply).

If other gases are present, verify whether a gas analyzer is installed in the regenerator exhaust vent upstream of any addition (and upstream of a CO boiler) that measures CO2, CO, and O2 continuously (required for §63.1573(a)(2)).

Verify the locations of measurement relative to downstream equipment (e.g., electrostatic precipitator or carbon monoxide boiler) because §63.1573(a)(2) requires measuring upstream of a CO boiler and allows upstream or downstream of an ESP.

Confirm you have continuous parameter monitoring (or control room instrumentation) for volumetric air flow to the regenerator and gas temperature as required by §63.1573(a)(1)(i)–(ii) if using the air-flow/temperature alternative.

Decide whether you will elect Option 1b or Option 2 in §63.1564(a)(1) (coke burn-off or PM per coke burn-off) because use of the NESHAP equations to compute PM emission rates is linked to those options.

Check whether your current performance-test procedures rely on Method 2 for Qsd and, if you propose the alternative, prepare the documentation showing you meet the conditions of §63.1573(a)(1) or (2) and include those calculations in the performance-test report per §63.1564(b)(4)(i).

Determine whether any approval from the Administrator or delegated permitting authority is required for alternative monitoring or to include the alternative procedure in your Notification of Compliance Status and operation, maintenance, and monitoring plan (see §63.1573(f) and §63.1574(f)).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If the affected source is a raw or finish mill, a raw material, clinker, or finished product storage bin, a conveying system transfer point, a bagging system, or a bulk loading/unloading system at a facility that is a major source subject to this subpart, then the owner/operator must not discharge any gases from these affected sources which exhibit opacity in excess of 10 percent.

If the affected source is a kiln or a clinker cooler, then Subpart LLL's Table 1 does not establish an opacity emissions limit for kilns or clinker coolers (Table 1 instead lists PM and other pollutant limits for kilns and clinker coolers), so an opacity limit is not set for those units by §63.1345.

If kiln exhaust and clinker cooler exhaust are combined (commingled) in a single stack and any contributing source to that commingled stream is subject to an opacity limit under §63.1345, then the owner/operator must demonstrate compliance with the opacity standard by conducting opacity performance testing using Method 9 as specified in §63.1349(b)(2) and by following the opacity monitoring procedures in §63.1350(f).

If the exhaust streams of a kiln with an in-line raw mill and a clinker cooler are comingled, then the commingled exhaust stream must be tested during performance tests with the raw mill both operating (mill on) and not operating (mill off).

If kiln gases are diverted through an alkali bypass or to an inline coal mill and exhausted through a separate stack (or some fraction of cooler or other exhaust bypasses the main kiln/raw mill stream), then pollutant-specific limits and compliance demonstrations (including calculation of kiln‑specific limits or alternative PM limits for commingled streams) must account for the diverted streams using the flow-weighted calculation procedures and alternative-limit equations in §63.1343(b)(2), §63.1349(b)(4)(iii), and §63.1349(b)(6)(iv).

checklist: Is the facility a major source or area source subject to Subpart LLL (verify applicability per §63.1340)?
Which specific units feed the common stack (identify kiln, clinker cooler, raw mill, finish mill, coal mill, alkali bypass, baghouse, etc.) and whether any of those unit types are listed in §63.1345?
Confirm whether the kiln is an in-line kiln/raw mill (can raw mill operate only with kiln) and whether clinker cooler exhaust is commingled with kiln exhaust in a single stack.

Quantify the fraction (by flow or mass) and the time fraction of clinker cooler exhaust that bypasses or does not pass through the in-line kiln/raw mill (you stated ~20% — have flow measurements or engineering estimates to support this).

Determine whether any diverted streams (alkali bypass, coal mill, or cooler bypass) exhaust to separate stacks or are recombined before the control device, and obtain volumetric flow rates (Qk, Qc, Qab, Qcm) for use in flow‑weighted calculations/equations referenced in §63.1343 and §63.1349.

Identify which pollutants and limits apply to each contributing source per Table 1 (PM, HCl, THC, D/F, mercury) so you can determine whether opacity testing/limits are triggered per §63.1345 and whether commingled testing/weighting is required per §63.1349.

Document control devices on the common stack (type, inlet temperatures, PM control device location) and whether the stack is downstream of the last control device (site-specific monitoring plan requirement under §63.1350(p)).

Verify existing monitoring systems and plans (COMS, Method 22 schedule, PM CPMS, CEMS/CPMS for HCl/THC/mercury, etc.) and readiness to perform Method 9 opacity tests per §63.1349(b)(2) and monitoring per §63.1350(f).

Collect records of prior performance tests, site-specific operating limits, and any time-weighting factors (mill on/off fractions) used previously for compliance calculations (per §§63.1348 and 63.1349).

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you apply surface coatings to miscellaneous metal parts or products and you use 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (and your facility is a major source or part of a major source), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If a given surface coating operation is performed using coatings that meet the definition of rubber-to-metal coatings (i.e., coatings that contain heat-activated polymer systems in solvent or water that dry to a non-tacky surface and react chemically with the rubber and metal during a vulcanization process), then that operation is in the rubber-to-metal coatings subcategory.

If a surface coating operation does not meet the definition of rubber-to-metal coatings (and does not meet the definitions for high performance, magnet wire, or extreme performance fluoropolymer subcategories), then that operation is in the general use coating subcategory.

If the facility uses only coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP as determined under the referenced methods, then the coating operations are not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you apply surface coatings to plastic parts or products and you use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (and your facility is a major source or part of a major source), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If a given surface coating operation on plastic parts is not an automotive lamp, TPO, or assembled on-road vehicle coating operation, then that operation is in the general use coating subcategory for Subpart PPPP.

If the facility uses only coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP as determined under the referenced methods, then the coating operations are not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Identify the substrate material for the coated parts (metal vs. plastic) for each coating operation.

Determine whether each coating formulation contains heat-activated polymer systems that dry to a non-tacky surface and chemically react with rubber and metal during a vulcanization process (i.e., whether bonding occurs via rubber vulcanization).
Document whether the bonding/curing step is a rubber vulcanization process or merely a heat cure that does not vulcanize rubber.
Collect manufacturer formulation data (or test data) showing whether coatings, thinners, additives, or cleaning materials contain organic HAP and the mass fraction of organic HAP.
Total annual volume (liters or gallons) of HAP-containing coatings used per affected coating operation and facility-wide (to compare with 946 L for MMMM and 378 L for PPPP thresholds).
Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tons of any single HAP or ≥25 tons total HAP per year).

Check whether the coating operation falls within any listed exclusions/subcategory definitions (e.g., magnet wire, high performance, TPO, automotive lamp, assembled on-road vehicle, or other exclusions in §63.3881(c) or §63.4481(c)).
Verify whether any coatings qualify as non-HAP coatings under the subpart definitions (e.g., ≤0.1% of listed organic HAP or ≤1.0% for other HAP).

candidates.title: Paper and Other Web Coating

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a major source of HAP and operates web coating lines, then the facility is subject to subpart JJJJ.

If a specific unit meets the definition of a web coating line (one or more work stations applying a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating between an unwind/feed station and a rewind or cutting station), then that unit is treated as a web coating line for purposes of subpart JJJJ.

If a web coating line is stand-alone equipment that the owner/operator includes in the affected source under subpart KK, then that web coating line is not part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ (i.e., is not subject to JJJJ as that line).

If a web coating line is a product and packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press that the owner/operator includes in the affected source under subpart KK, then that web coating line is not part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ.

If the web coating line is research or laboratory equipment (primary purpose research and development, operated under close supervision, and not engaged in commercial manufacture except de minimis), then the line is not part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ.

If a web coating line coats both paper or a web and another substrate, then the subpart that applies is the subpart for the predominant activity (predominant = 90 percent of mass of substrate coated during the compliance period) and JJJJ applies if the predominant activity is paper/web coating.

If all of the subject web coating lines at the facility utilize non-HAP coatings and the owner/operator submits the one-time report required in § 63.3370(s), then the facility can become exempt from the reporting requirements of subpart JJJJ.

candidates.title: Printing and Publishing Industry

criteria.criterion: If a web coating line is stand-alone equipment under subpart KK and the owner/operator includes it in the affected source under subpart KK, then that line is subject to subpart KK rather than being part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ.

If a web coating line is a product and packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press and the owner/operator includes it in the affected source under subpart KK, then that line is subject to subpart KK rather than being part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ.

If the web coating line performs printing-type web coating processes (e.g., lithography, screenprinting, letterpress, narrow-web flexographic printing), then those printing web coating lines are not part of the affected source under subpart JJJJ and are candidates for subpart KK (or other printing subparts).

If a web coating line with product and packaging rotogravure and/or wide-web flexographic print station(s) has the mass of materials applied to its print station(s) ever exceed 5 percent of the total mass of materials applied onto the line in a month, then the owner/operator may elect to continue demonstrating compliance with subpart JJJJ instead of subpart KK.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAP (check permitting/major-source determination).

Confirm whether the process meets the definition of a web coating line: unwind/feed station, one or more work stations that apply continuous liquid or semi-liquid coating (including adhesives), any associated curing/drying equipment, and a rewind or cutting station (see 40 CFR 63.3310).
Identify the coating materials used (adhesives/glues); confirm that adhesives are considered 'coating materials' under § 63.3310.

For each line, determine whether it is stand-alone printing/press equipment that is included under subpart KK (e.g., product & packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press) or whether it is a non-printing web coating line (check equipment type and how owner/operator has previously designated affected sources).

If any print stations exist, calculate monthly mass of materials applied to print stations and the total mass applied to the line to see if print-station mass ever exceeds 5% of the line total in any month.

If the line coats multiple substrates, determine the mass fraction by substrate (over a reasonable period of at least one year or other representative period) to establish whether paper/web coating is the predominant activity (≥90% by mass) per § 63.3300(h).
Determine whether any equipment is research or laboratory equipment as defined in § 63.3310 (primary purpose research and development, not commercial manufacture except de minimis).

Verify whether all coatings used are 'non-HAP' under § 63.3370(s) (organic HAP <0.1% by mass for OSHA-defined carcinogens and <1.0% by mass for other organic HAP); if so, prepare the one-time report required by § 63.3370(s) to claim reporting exemption.

If planning to comply via controls, identify whether a solvent recovery system, oxidizer, or other add-on control will be used (applicability affects monitoring and demonstration procedures described in § 63.3370 and § 63.3350).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Printing, Coating, Slashing, Dyeing, and Finishing of Fabrics and Other Textiles

criteria.criterion: If the facility conducts printing, coating, slashing, dyeing, or finishing of fabric or other textiles and the operation is an affected source that is a major source (or is located at or part of a major source of HAP), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If the tipping or other operation does not meet the subpart definitions of coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing of fabric or other textiles (per the definitions in §63.4371), then the operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the operation uses only regulated materials that contain no organic HAP (as defined in §63.4371 and Table 5 to this subpart), then the coating/printing/slashing/dyeing/finishing operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the web coating/printing, slashing, or dyeing/finishing operation is conducted at ambient temperatures and does not involve drying or curing equipment such as ovens, tenter frames, steam cans, or dryers, then that operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the equipment and materials used in the operation match the elements listed for an affected source in §63.4282(b) (for web coating and printing) or the analogous lists for slashing or dyeing/finishing, then those items are part of the affected source and subject to this subpart.

If a web coating line coats both fabric/textiles and other substrates, then the applicable subpart is determined by the predominant activity (90 percent of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period); if the predominant activity is another substrate, this subpart may not apply.
If the operation is performed by the facility and not for commerce and organic HAP emissions from the operation are below major source thresholds, then the operation is not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the shoelace tipping operation fits the regulatory definitions of coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing in 40 CFR 63.4371 (e.g., does it apply a semi-liquid that forms a continuous film (coating) or chemically impregnate the fiber (finishing), or is it only a minor surface wetting?).
Determine whether shoelaces/cords produced are 'fabric' or 'textile' under 40 CFR 63.4371 (definitions include thread and yarn).

Verify whether the methanol solution and any other materials used contain any organic HAP (check material formulation data and Table 5 to this subpart or supplier/manufacturer information to determine organic HAP content and the 'no organic HAP' thresholds).
Confirm whether the tipping operation uses drying or curing equipment (ovens, tenter frames, steam cans, dryers) or is performed at ambient temperature without such equipment.

Establish whether the facility (or the affected source that would include the tipping operation) is a major source of HAP or is located at / part of a major source of HAP (check total HAP potential to emit against major source thresholds).
Identify whether the operation is conducted for commerce (commercial production) or only for on-site/noncommercial use.

Inventory the pieces of equipment and materials used in the operation and compare to the affected source component lists in 40 CFR 63.4282(b) (e.g., application equipment, drying/curing equipment, storage containers, mixing vessels, waste handling, wastewater treatment) to see if the tipping operation would be part of an affected source.

If the same line or equipment also coats other substrates (paper, etc.), measure the mass of each substrate coated during the compliance period to determine the predominant substrate by mass (90% test) for subpart assignment.

If the surface coating operation meets any of the exclusions in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(5) (for example, certain plywood/composite wood manufacturing processes subject to subpart DDDD, wood furniture subject to subpart JJ, prefabricated homes, research/laboratory/hobby noncommercial operations, or wood treatment by impregnation), then not subject

If surface coating operations at the affected source that are subject to another subpart account for at least 95 percent of the total annual coating usage for the affected source, then you may comply with that other subpart for the entire affected source (then not subject to this subpart)

If the material applied is an adhesive (a chemical substance applied for the purpose of bonding two surfaces together) and it is used in coating operations on wood building products, then the material is considered a coating for purposes of this subpart and the operation is subject

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If the operation is surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products (which expressly includes items such as extruded aluminum structural components) and the affected source uses 946 liters (250 gallons) or more per year of coatings that contain HAP and is a major source (or located at/part of a major source of HAP), then subject

If the coatings applied meet the definition of high performance architectural coating (e.g., coatings that meet AAMA 605.2-2000) or otherwise meet the 'high performance coating' definition, then the operation is in the high performance coating subcategory of this subpart and is subject

If the surface coating is of metal components of wood building products that meet the applicability criteria for wood building products surface coating (subpart QQQQ), then not subject to this subpart
If the facility uses only coatings, thinners, other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (as determined under the cited provisions), then not subject to this subpart

If individual coatings are used in volumes of less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings qualifying under this small-volume provision does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then not subject (for those coatings/operations)

checklist: For wood components: confirm the product is a 'wood building product' (contains >50% wood or wood fiber by weight, excluding glass, and is used in building construction).
For wood components: determine whether the items coated are windows/window components or other items listed in the doors, windows, and miscellaneous subcategory.
For wood components: measure total annual volume of all coatings used at the affected source (liters per year) and verify if it is ≥4,170 L/yr.
For wood components: determine whether the facility is a major HAP source (potential to emit ≥10 tpy for any single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).

For wood components: verify whether the operation falls into any exclusion in 63.4681(c) (plywood/composite manufacturing processes, wood furniture/cabinet millwork subject to subpart JJ, prefabricated home operations, research/lab/hobby noncommercial, or pressure impregnation/retort wood treatment).

For wood components: identify whether adhesives are used as part of the coating/laminating/finishing operations and classify those adhesives (manufacturer formulation/HAP content, reactive adhesives vs. conventional).

For wood components: collect formulation/manufacturer data or test results needed to calculate organic HAP content and volume fraction of coating solids if using the compliant-material option per 63.4741.

For metal (aluminum) components: confirm the parts are miscellaneous metal parts/products (e.g., extruded aluminum structural components, aluminum window components) and not metal components of wood building products covered by QQQQ.
For metal components: determine whether the coatings used are HAP-containing or qualify as non-HAP coatings (do not count non-HAP coatings toward the 946 L applicability threshold).
For metal components: measure total annual volume of HAP-containing coatings used at the affected source (liters per year) and verify if it is ≥946 L/yr.

For metal components: determine whether the applied coatings meet the definition of high performance architectural coating (e.g., AAMA 605.2-2000) or other specific subcategory definitions in 63.3981.
For metal components: determine whether any small-volume exemptions apply (individual coatings <189 L/yr and total exempt coatings ≤946 L/yr).
For metal components: determine whether the facility is a major HAP source (potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).

For either operation: determine whether another surface-coating NESHAP covers coating operations that account for ≥95% of total annual coating usage (to consider complying under that other subpart instead).

For either operation: assemble supplier/manufacturer formulation data or test results to show organic HAP content, coating solids, and density for compliance demonstrations and threshold calculations.

candidates.title: Site Remediation (Site Remediation MACT)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a facility that conducts a site remediation (as defined in § 63.7957) and the site remediation (1) cleans up a remediation material, (2) is co-located at your facility with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition for a source category regulated by another subpart under 40 CFR part 63, and (3) your facility is a major source of HAP, then the site remediation is subject to this subpart
if your site remediation only cleans up material that does not contain any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart
if your site remediation is conducted at a gasoline service station to clean up remediation material from a leaking underground storage tank, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart
if your site remediation is conducted at a farm or residential site, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart
if your site remediation is conducted at a research and development facility that meets the requirements under CAA section 112(c)(7), then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart

if the total quantity of the HAP listed in Table 1 contained in the remediation material excavated, extracted, pumped, or otherwise removed during all site remediations at your facility is less than 1 megagram (Mg) annually and you prepare and maintain written documentation supporting that determination, then the site remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart (except for the recordkeeping requirement)

if all remediation activities at your facility that would be subject to this subpart are completed and you have notified the Administrator in writing that all remediation activities subject to this subpart are completed, then those remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart (subject to recordkeeping obligations)

if a site remediation is completed within 30 consecutive calendar days according to the initiation and completion definitions and shipping/ documentation conditions in § 63.7884(b), then that site remediation is not subject to the standards in § 63.7884(a)

if a remediation material management unit is part of an affected source and you determine the average total VOHAP concentration of the remediation material managed in the unit is less than 500 ppmw (demonstrated per § 63.7943), then that remediation material management unit meets the requirements of § 63.7886(b)(2) (i.e., is not required to meet the air‑pollution‑control options in § 63.7886(b)(1))

if a process vent treats or vents remediation material whose average total VOHAP concentration is less than 10 ppmw (determined per § 63.7943), then that process vent meets the provision in § 63.7885(b)(2) and is not required to meet the control options in § 63.7885(b)(1)

if an equipment component contains or contacts remediation material having a concentration of total HAP listed in Table 1 equal to or greater than 10 percent by weight and the component is intended to operate for 300 hours or more during a calendar year in remediation material service, then that component is part of the affected equipment‑leaks source and is subject to the equipment‑leak provisions of this subpart

if a process vent stream flow rate is less than 0.005 m3/min at standard conditions, or if the flow rate is less than 6.0 m3/min and the total concentration of HAP listed in Table 1 is less than 20 ppmv, then the process vent is exempt from the requirements of § 63.7885(b)

if a surface impoundment is an affected remediation material management unit under § 63.7886(b)(1)(iii), then you must control HAP emissions by installing and operating either a floating membrane cover per § 63.942 or a cover vented through a closed vent system to a control device per § 63.943 (and meet the closed‑vent/control device work practice limits in § 63.7925)

checklist: Determine whether the planned excavation/backfill activity meets the subpart's definition of site remediation and whether the excavated soil qualifies as 'remediation material' (see § 63.7957 definitions for soil and remediation material).
Determine whether the excavated soil contains any HAP listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG (perform speciation/testing as needed and document methods and data).

Calculate annual total quantity (mass) of HAP in all remediation materials excavated at the facility this year to verify if it is ≥ or < 1 Mg/yr (facility‑wide, cumulative across all site remediations).

Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAP (PTE or actual emissions ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy aggregate HAP) and whether the site remediation is co‑located with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected‑source definition under another Part 63 subpart.

If claiming the 30‑day exemption, document the initiation date (first action that manages remediation material), completion date (treatment/disposal such that volatilization potential is eliminated), and whether shipped off‑site materials were transferred within 30 days with required shipping documentation.

If relying on the <1 Mg exemption for units you wish to exempt, identify and mark or notify the Administrator of the exempt remediation material management units and prepare the initial determination and documentation of annual HAP quantity placed in those units.

If the excavated soil will be stored or managed in a remediation material management unit, identify the type of unit (tank, container, surface impoundment, separator, transfer system) and whether the unit will be subject to the control options or eligible for the VOHAP <500 ppmw path.

Measure or estimate average total VOHAP concentration of the remediation material at the point where material is placed in the management unit (to evaluate the <500 ppmw path) and for any material vented to process vents (to evaluate the <10 ppmw path).

Identify any process vents associated with the remediation activity, measure their stream flow rates and total HAP concentrations to determine applicability of the flow‑rate/ concentration exemptions (0.005 m3/min or <6.0 m3/min with <20 ppmv HAP).

Inventory equipment components that will contact the remediation material and verify for each: the total HAP concentration in the contacted material (≥10% or <10% by weight) and the expected operating hours per year (≥300 hours or <300 hours) to determine equipment‑leak affected‑source status.

If surface impoundment(s) will be used, confirm whether you will install and operate the required floating membrane cover or a cover vented through a closed vent system to a control device and prepare to meet the referenced control device/closed‑vent work practice standards.

Prepare and retain required written documentation supporting any determinations or exemptions (VOHAP results, <1 Mg calculations, 30‑day initiation/completion records, process vent flow tests, and equipment‑leak membership) and be ready to include required statements in the Notification of Compliance Status per § 63.7937 as applicable.

candidates.title: Organic Liquid Distribution (OLD) operations — national emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an organic liquid distribution (OLD) operation that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP emissions, then the OLD operation is subject to this subpart EEEE.

If the activity involves the collection of activities and equipment used to distribute organic liquids into, out of, or within a facility (including storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles while loading/unloading, and containers while loading/unloading at transfer racks), then those items are part of the affected source under this subpart.

If a container, transfer rack, transport vehicle, or other equipment is non-permanent and is being used in a special-situation distribution loading or unloading operation (such as maintenance or upset liquids management), then that non-permanent equipment is excluded from the affected source (i.e., excluded from subpart coverage for that use).

If a transfer rack only unloads organic liquids (i.e., no loading into transport vehicles or containers occurs at that rack), then that transfer rack is an emission source identified in §63.2338 that is not required to be controlled under the emission-control provisions of this subpart and must have documentation verifying that status.

If the liquid being transferred meets the subpart's definition of an "organic liquid" (e.g., contains >= 5 percent by weight of the organic HAP in Table 1 or is a crude oil/condensate downstream of the first point of custody transfer), then the liquid is within the scope of OLD operations for this subpart.

If your storage tanks or transfer racks meet the tank capacity, vapor pressure, or facility-level loading volume control criteria in Table 2 (or Table 2b) to this subpart, then you must comply with the emission limits, operating limits, or specified work practice standards in §63.2346 (including associated referenced requirements).

candidates.title: Referenced subpart SS — applicable requirements for meeting emission limits for storage tanks and transfer racks

criteria.criterion: If you elect or are required to meet the emission limits specified in Table 2 (or Table 2b) for storage tanks or transfer racks, then you must comply with the applicable requirements specified in subpart SS for meeting those emission limits (substitute the term "storage tank" where applicable).

candidates.title: Referenced subpart TT — equipment leak control level 1 (as referenced by subpart EEEE)

criteria.criterion: If a pump, valve, or sampling connection operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year at an affected source that has at least one storage tank or transfer rack meeting the control applicability criteria, and you are subject to control at control level 1, then the equipment leak components must comply with the applicable requirements under subpart TT.

candidates.title: Referenced subpart UU — equipment leak control level 2 (as referenced by subpart EEEE)

criteria.criterion: If a pump, valve, or sampling connection operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year at an affected source that has at least one storage tank or transfer rack meeting the control applicability criteria, and you are subject to control at control level 2, then the equipment leak components must comply with the applicable requirements under subpart UU.

checklist: Is your refinery an HAP major source (potential to emit or actual emissions meet the CAA major-source threshold)?

Are the transfers (container-to-container via gravity/non-permanent hoses/valves; truck-to-container with or without pump) part of the facility's routine OLD operations (i.e., distribution into, out of, or within the plant site) rather than special-situation/maintenance/upset operations?
Do the liquids transferred meet the subpart's "organic liquid" definition (contain >=5 wt% of Table 1 organic HAP or are crude/condensate downstream of first custody transfer)?

Are the transfers occurring at a transfer rack as defined (a single system used to load into or unload out of transport vehicles or containers), or are they isolated portable/container-to-container transfers not associated with a transfer rack?

Are containers, hoses, or valves used permanent parts of the transfer rack/transfer system or non-permanent; if non-permanent, are they being used in routine distribution or only in special-situation operations?
Does the transfer operation involve loading into transport vehicles (truck/cargo tanks) or only unloading? (If only unloading, different documentation/control requirements apply per §63.2343(a)).

What are the storage tank capacities and annual average true vapor pressures, and what is the facility-level annual organic liquid loading volume (3-year rolling average) — compare these to Table 2 / Table 2b control criteria to determine whether control requirements apply?

For transport vehicles: do they have vapor-collection equipment and current U.S. DOT certification (49 CFR part 180 subpart E/F) or have they passed Method 27 vapor-tight tests as required when transfer racks are subject to control?

If equipment leaks (pumps/valves/sampling connectors) are present, do any operate in organic liquids service >=300 hours/year, and if so, which control level (subpart TT, UU, or H) will be applicable?

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing (NESHAP: subpart HHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations that (1) are located at or part of a major source of HAP, (2) manufacture coatings, (3) process, use, or produce HAP, and (4) are not part of an affected source under another subpart, then the operations are subject to this subpart.

If a tank or other vessel (stationary or portable) has a capacity greater than or equal to 250 gallons and is used for mixing, blending, diluting, dissolving, temporary holding, or other processing in the manufacturing of a coating, then it is a 'process vessel' and is included in the miscellaneous coating manufacturing affected source.
If a vessel has a capacity less than 250 gallons, then it is not a 'process vessel' under this subpart.
If you are an existing affected source and you seek to use the emissions-averaging alternative, then that alternative applies only to stationary process vessels greater than or equal to 250 gallons.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (NESHAP: subpart MMMM)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP for surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the facility is a major source (or is located at or part of a major source), then the facility is subject to this subpart.

If you are subject to this subpart, then the affected source includes all storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners, and/or other additives, and cleaning materials are stored or mixed (regardless of individual vessel capacity).

If a coating operation uses less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year of coatings, and the total volume of coatings exempt under this provision does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then that coating operation is excluded from this subpart.

candidates.title: Large Appliance Surface Coating (NESHAP: subpart NNNN)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source as defined in this subpart (i.e., a large appliance surface coating facility), then the affected source includes all storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials are stored or mixed.

checklist: Measure the mixer capacity in gallons (is it <250 gal or ≥250 gal?).
Confirm whether the mixer is stationary or portable and whether it is used for mixing/blending/diluting/temporary holding in manufacturing of coatings.
Determine whether the material processed in the mixer is a 'coating' as defined in 40 CFR 63.8105/63.3981 (resins, pigments, solvents, additives; produced by blending/mixing/formulating).
Determine whether the coatings/materials handled contain HAP (and which HAP) and whether the facility processes, uses, or produces HAP.
Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).
Calculate annual facility usage of coatings containing HAP (gallons per year) to check the 946 L (250 gal/yr) threshold used in subpart MMMM.
For any single coating operation, determine annual usage (is it <189 L/50 gal/yr?) and the total of such exempt operations (does total exempt ≤946 L/250 gal/yr?).

Determine whether the mixer or its emissions are already part of an affected source under another subpart (e.g., MMMM, NNNN, or other surface-coating NESHAP) to evaluate the 'not part of an affected source under another subpart' condition in 63.7985(a)(4).
If claiming the HHHHH emissions-averaging alternative, verify whether the vessel is stationary and ≥250 gallons (eligibility requirement in 63.8050(a)).
Identify whether the mixer is used only to modify a purchased coating in preparation for application at the purchasing facility (exclusion in 63.7985(d)(5)).
Document whether mixing operations produce process vessel vents or are routed to control devices (relevance for control/monitoring requirements in 63.8005 and related provisions).

candidates.title: Surface coating of metal furniture

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of metal furniture as defined in §63.4881(a) and you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source as defined in §63.4882 that is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP, then you are subject to this subpart.
If the surface coating conducted at an affected source uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then this subpart does not apply to that surface coating.
If the surface coating is of metal components of wood furniture and is conducted in an operation subject to the wood furniture manufacturing NESHAP in subpart JJ, then this subpart does not apply.
If the surface coating occurs at research or laboratory facilities or is part of janitorial, building, and facility maintenance operations, then this subpart does not apply.

If the surface coating is of only small items such as knobs, hinges, or screws that have a wider use beyond metal furniture and the coating does not occur at an affected metal furniture source, then this subpart does not apply.

If the surface coating is conducted solely for repairing or maintaining metal furniture used by a major source and not for commerce, then this subpart does not apply unless the organic HAP emissions from the coating itself are as high as the major-source emission rates specified in paragraph (b).
If the surface coating is performed on-site at installations owned or operated by the Armed Forces of the United States, then this subpart does not apply.

If your operations include the items listed in §63.4882(b) (all coating operations, storage containers and mixing vessels for coatings/thinners/cleaning materials, conveying equipment and associated pumps and piping, and storage and conveying of waste materials from coating operations), then those items constitute the affected source for applicability under this subpart.

If you intend to rely on the compliant material option to demonstrate that you use no organic HAP-containing materials, then you must determine the mass fraction (and where applicable volume fraction and density) of organic HAP for each coating, thinner, and cleaning material using one of the methods listed in §63.4941(a) (e.g., Method 311, Method 24, manufacturer formulation data, or approved alternative) and retain the records required by §63.4941(e).

checklist: Confirm whether the items you coat (stainless steel cabinetry, parts, components) meet the regulatory definition of "metal furniture" (examples in §63.4881(a)).
Determine whether your facility is a major HAP source (potential to emit any single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or any combination ≥ 25 tpy).

Inventory every coating, thinner, thinner blend, cleaning material, and adhesive currently used and verify whether each contains any organic HAP (use Method 311, Method 24, manufacturer formulation data, or other approved method per §63.4941(a)).

For each coating, determine mass fraction of organic HAP and volume fraction of coating solids (and density) per the procedures in §63.4941(b)–(d) to document that organic HAP content is zero or below applicable limits if claiming the exclusion or using the compliant-material option.
Verify whether coating operations include storage/mixing vessels, pumps/piping, conveying equipment, or waste collection that would be part of the affected source per §63.4882(b).

Confirm whether any coating activity falls under the exclusions: wood-furniture components subject to subpart JJ; research/laboratory; janitorial/building/facility maintenance; small items not coated at an affected metal furniture source; repair/maintenance for in-house use only; or on-site Armed Forces installations (see §63.4881(c)(1)–(6)).

If you previously used methylene chloride or other organic HAPs, confirm you have discontinued their use and that any reclaimed cleaning materials were demonstrated as HAP-free in the condition received (see §63.4941(e)).

If relying on the compliant-material exclusion or option, compile and retain the initial compliance demonstration and ongoing monthly/semiannual records and statements required by §§63.4940–63.4942 and §63.4941(e).
Determine whether your source is new, reconstructed, or existing (per §63.4882(c)–(e)) and note applicable compliance dates for initial demonstration per §63.4940.

candidates.title: Secondary Lead Smelting MACT (secondary lead smelters)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate any of the affected sources listed (blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; process fugitive emissions sources; buildings containing lead-bearing materials; or fugitive dust sources) at a secondary lead smelter, then you are subject to this subpart.
If you are a primary lead processor, lead refiner, or lead remelter, then you are not subject to this subpart.

If your facility does not perform smelting (i.e., does not chemically reduce lead compounds to elemental lead or lead alloys in high-temperature furnaces, as defined) and therefore does not meet the definition of a 'secondary lead smelter', then this subpart does not apply to your facility.

If you operate affected sources at a secondary lead smelter, then being below the numeric lead emission limits does not by itself remove your facility from applicability and you remain subject to the subpart's requirements and compliance/monitoring/recordkeeping obligations.

checklist: Do you operate any smelting furnace(s) (blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric) or other affected sources listed in §63.541(a) (refining kettles, agglomerating furnaces, dryers, process fugitive sources, buildings containing lead-bearing materials, fugitive dust sources)?
Does your process perform smelting as defined in §63.542 (chemical reduction of lead compounds to elemental lead or lead alloys in high‑temperature furnaces >980 °C)?
Is the facility recycling lead‑bearing scrap by smelting (i.e., functioning as a secondary lead smelter) rather than only performing mechanical or glass‑only recycling processes?
Is your facility instead a primary lead processor, lead refiner, or lead remelter (activities that would exclude you under §63.541(a))?
Does the material you handle meet the definition of lead‑bearing material (lead content threshold per EPA Method 1311 as referenced in §63.542)?

Which specific vents, stacks, baghouses, building ventilation systems, total enclosures, and fugitive dust sources do you have that could be 'process vents', 'process fugitive emissions sources', or 'fugitive dust sources' as listed in §63.541(a) and §63.542?

Do you currently monitor or measure lead emissions from process vents (and can you document concentrations and flow rates) and do you already meet or plan to meet the monitoring/recordkeeping requirements (e.g., CEMS, bag leak detection, total enclosure differential pressure) described in §§63.543, 63.548, and 63.550?

candidates.title: General Provisions (recordkeeping and reporting)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to 40 CFR part 63 then they must maintain files of all information required by this part in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious inspection and retain the files for at least 5 years with the most recent 2 years kept on site, and the remaining 3 years may be off site.

candidates.title: Recordkeeping requirements for storage vessels (Subpart WW)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate external floating roof storage vessels covered by Subpart WW then you must keep the records specified in §63.1065 (including vessel dimensions and identification, floating roof inspection results, and EFR seal gap measurements including the raw data and any calculations) with vessel-dimension records kept as long as liquid is stored and the records in paragraphs (b),(c),(d) kept at least 5 years and made readily accessible within 24 hours.

candidates.title: Recordkeeping requirements (Subpart DD)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to Subpart DD then they must comply with the recordkeeping requirements of §63.10 (the General Provisions) as specified in §63.696.

If an owner or operator uses an external floating roof to comply with the tank control requirements specified in §63.685(f) of Subpart DD then they must prepare and maintain records for each seal gap inspection that include the date the measurements are performed, the raw data obtained, and the calculations of total gap surface area.

candidates.title: What records must I keep? (Subpart HHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to Subpart HHHHHH then they must keep the records specified in §63.11990 (including the storage-vessel records described in paragraph (b)) and other documentation supporting notifications and reports.

If an owner or operator has internal or external floating roof storage vessels subject to Subpart HHHHHH then they must maintain the records required in §63.1065 of Subpart WW for internal and external floating roof storage vessels.

checklist: Identify which NESHAP subpart(s) (e.g., WW, DD, HHHHHH or others) your storage tanks are regulated under for your facility.
Confirm whether each tank is an external floating roof tank (EFR) and whether compliance is demonstrated under the specific tank-control provisions of a given subpart (e.g., §63.685(f)).
Verify that EFR seal-gap measurement records include the raw measurement data and any calculations (not just summary values) for each inspection.
Verify that vessel-dimensions and capacity records are retained for as long as the liquid is stored (if required by the applicable subpart).
Confirm the retention period applicable to each required record (e.g., some records kept as long as liquid is stored; others kept at least 5 years) based on the specific subpart citations.

Confirm that the most recent 2 years of required records are physically on site or readily accessible from on site (e.g., via on-site computer network) and that remaining years are retained per the applicable rule.

Confirm that any electronic records you rely on after discarding field notes are complete, include the raw data and calculations, and are in a format that can be produced within 24 hours for inspection.

If you transfer field notes into an electronic form and discard paper notes, document the transfer (who, when, method) and ensure the electronic version meets the raw-data requirement in the applicable subpart.
Check whether any specific subpart requires retention of original or superseded plan versions (e.g., site-specific monitoring plans) and retain those as required.

If you submit records electronically to EPA (e.g., via CEDRI), confirm whether the subpart allows electronic maintenance and whether on-site availability requirements are still met (keep evidence of accessibility).
