candidates.title: Area Sources: Carbon Black Production

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a carbon black production facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then you are subject to this subpart

if you own or operate a new or existing carbon black production process unit then this subpart applies to each affected source (each carbon black production process unit) including all waste management units, maintenance wastewater, and equipment components that contain or contact HAP associated with the process unit
if your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act then this subpart does not apply to you

candidates.title: Source category-specific applicability, definitions, and requirements (includes Carbon Black Production provisions)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a carbon black production process unit located at a major source of HAP emissions then the affected source is each carbon black production process unit and the carbon black production provisions of this section apply

if your activities meet the definition of carbon black production (production of carbon black by the furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes) then the carbon black production definitions and affected-source scope in this paragraph apply

if the HAP concentration of a carbon black production main unit filter process vent or other carbon black production process vent is equal to or greater than 260 parts per million by volume (as determined using the process vent applicability determination procedures) then the process vent is subject to the Table 8 requirements (e.g., route to a flare or achieve 98 weight-percent reduction or equivalent limits) under the carbon black production requirements

candidates.title: Applicability and designation of affected sources for off-site material waste management and recovery operations

criteria.criterion: if the plant site is a major source of HAP emissions and the plant site includes one or more operations that receive off-site materials and those operations are one of the listed waste management or recovery operations (e.g., recovery/reprocessing of off-site material) then the provisions of this subpart apply to the owner/operator of the plant site

if the material you manage is an off-site material (i.e., a waste, used oil, or used solvent not produced on-site, delivered from outside the plant site, and containing one or more HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart at the point-of-delivery) then that material is governed by this subpart for the listed operations

if the total annual quantity of the HAP contained in off-site material received at the plant site is less than 1 megagram per year then the owner/operator is exempted from the requirements of §§ 63.682 through 63.699 of this subpart

candidates.title: General Provisions (selected §§ 63.1–63.5 and §§ 63.11–63.16) as applied to this subpart

criteria.criterion: if you are subject to Subpart MMMMMM then the General Provisions in 40 CFR part 63, subpart A, §§ 63.1 through 63.5 and §§ 63.11 through 63.16 apply to your obligations under that subpart

checklist: Determine whether your facility is an area source or a major source of HAPs (potential to emit a single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined HAPs ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy))

Determine whether your process meets the definition of 'carbon black production' (production of carbon black by furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes) or is instead only mechanical/thermal reclamation not covered by that definition

Identify each process unit used to recover carbon black/oil/steel (reactors, dryers, main unit filter, product vents, tailgas, recovery devices) to decide if they are 'carbon black production process unit(s)'
If you claim the R&D exclusion, verify that the facility meets the Clean Air Act §112(c)(7) research and development definition

Determine whether the plant receives off‑site material (e.g., tires delivered from off-site) and, if so, quantify the annual mass of HAP in off-site material to see if it exceeds 1 megagram/year (for Subpart DD exemption)

Measure or estimate HAP concentration in main unit filter and other process vent streams (use the applicability determination procedures referenced in 63.1103(f)(3)(iv)) to determine if any vent stream is ≥260 ppmv

Establish whether the process units were constructed/reconstructed before or after the dates that distinguish 'existing' vs 'new' (e.g., for Subpart MMMMMM existing if commenced on or before April 4, 2007) to determine applicable compliance dates
Confirm whether the facility is part of or co-located with any rubber tire manufacturing operations or other sources that would change the source classification (e.g., make the plant a major source)
Document whether any vents are routed to boilers/process heaters or flares (since routing affects applicable tune-up and control requirements under the carbon black provisions)
Gather process flow diagrams, material receipts (origin of tires), and emission estimates to support applicability determinations and any required applicability testing or reporting

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you perform surface coating of plastic parts and products as defined in this subpart, and you use 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants, and the affected source is a major source of HAP, then the source is subject to this subpart.
If your facility uses only coatings, thinners and other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then the surface coating operation is not subject to this subpart.

If you elect the emission rate with add-on controls compliance option, then you must include emissions reductions from emission capture systems and add-on controls and ensure those capture systems and add-on controls meet the operating limits in § 63.4492, the work practice standards in § 63.4493, and the procedural requirements in §§ 63.4560 through 63.4568 to demonstrate compliance.

If you use an add-on control device other than those listed in Table 1 to this subpart (for example a device not listed in Table 1 such as a boiler, if not listed), then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f).

If you use an add-on control device that is not a solvent recovery system using liquid-liquid material balances, then you must calculate organic HAP emission reductions by applying the emission capture system efficiency and the add-on control device destruction or removal efficiency (DRE) to the mass of organic HAP used, with capture efficiency and DRE measured and recorded as required when demonstrating initial compliance and continuous compliance, and you must assume zero efficiency during any deviation unless you have other data approved by the Administrator.

If you use a solvent recovery system for control and elect to conduct a liquid-liquid material balance, then you must perform the monthly liquid-liquid material balance procedures and determine the volatile organic matter collection and recovery efficiency as specified for solvent recovery systems.

checklist: Confirm the operations are surface coating of plastic parts and products (methods of application, associated prep/cleaning) per the subpart definition.
Record annual volume (liters or gallons) of coatings that contain any HAP to confirm whether usage is ≥ 378 L (100 gal) per year.
Determine whether the affected source is a major source of HAP (≥ 10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥ 25 tpy total HAP).
Inventory all coatings, thinners/additives, and cleaning materials to determine organic HAP content (identify presence of methanol).
Decide which compliance option will be used for each coating operation (compliant material; emission rate without add-on controls; emission rate with add-on controls).

If planning the emission rate with add-on controls option, identify which coating operations will be controlled and whether any operations will instead use compliant-material or emission-rate-without-controls options.

If you intend to use a boiler as the add-on control, check Table 1 for whether boilers are listed as an approved control device for the applicable coating category; if not listed, prepare an application for alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f).
Document how emissions will be captured and routed to the boiler (capture system design) and prepare to measure or estimate capture efficiency for the capture system serving the coating operation.

Assess whether the boiler can be tested to determine its destruction/removal efficiency (DRE) for organic HAP and plan performance testing to establish operating limits during the required performance tests.

If using solvent recovery instead of combustion, confirm you can install and certify the device to measure cumulative volatile organic matter recovered monthly and perform the liquid-liquid material balance procedures.

Prepare a work practice plan per § 63.4493 (closed containers, minimize spills, closed transfer, closed mixing vessels, minimizing emissions during cleaning) if using the emission rate with add-on controls option.

Plan recordkeeping and monthly rolling 12-month emission rate calculations and be prepared to treat emissions as uncontrolled (zero control efficiency) during any deviations unless alternative data are approved by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Engine Test Cells and Stands (NESHAP, Subpart PPPPP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions then that engine test cell/stand is subject to this subpart.

If your plant emits or has the potential to emit a single HAP at a rate of 10 tons per year or more or any combination of HAP at a rate of 25 tons per year or more then the plant is a major source for purposes of this subpart.

If you commenced construction of the affected source on or before May 14, 2002 then the affected source is an existing affected source, and if you commenced construction of the affected source after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a new affected source.

If you meet the definition of reconstruction in § 63.2 and reconstruction was commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a reconstructed affected source (and reconstruction is evaluated per § 63.2), and passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics are not included in the reconstruction evaluation.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power less than 25 horsepower (19 kW) then that portion does not have to meet the subpart requirements except for the initial notification requirement.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, non-commercial research and teaching, or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics, then that portion does not have to meet the subpart requirements.

If your affected source is new or reconstructed and is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of 25 hp (19 kW) or more at a major source then you must comply with the emission limitations in Table 1 for new or reconstructed affected sources.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) - Definitions and Reconstruction/Commenced rules

criteria.criterion: If the replacement of components of an affected source results in fixed capital costs of the new components that exceed 50 percent of the fixed capital cost to construct a comparable new source and it is technologically and economically feasible for the reconstructed source to meet relevant standards, then the activity meets the definition of reconstruction.

If an owner or operator has undertaken a continuous program of construction or has entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete, within a reasonable time, a continuous program of construction or reconstruction, then construction or reconstruction is considered to have been commenced.

If equipment replaced is minor ancillary equipment (for example piping, ductwork, valves), then the costs of replacing that minor ancillary equipment must be considered in determining whether the existing affected source is reconstructed.
citations: 40 CFR 63.2 (The costs of replacing minor ancillary equipment must be considered...)

candidates.title: Subpart KK (selected provision on reconstruction and cost treatment)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source has undergone reconstruction then it is subject to the requirements for new affected sources under this subpart.

If costs are associated with the purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment, or are costs for retrofitting or replacement of equipment installed specifically to comply with this subpart, then those costs are not considered in determining whether the affected source has been reconstructed.

checklist: Total annual actual and potential HAP emissions for the plant (single-HAP tpy and combined HAP tpy) to determine major source status.
Inventory of all engine test cells/stands and confirmation that tested engines are uninstalled (definition of engine test cell/stand and uninstalled engine).
Rated power (hp or kW) of engines tested in each cell/stand to determine applicability of the ≥25 hp threshold.

Dates for all construction, replacements, additions, and modifications to test cells/stands (purchase orders, installation dates, contracts, project plans) to compare against May 14, 2002 and to document whether work was part of a continuous program or contractual obligation.

Documented cost breakdown for replaced or added components (fixed capital costs for new components) and methodology/assumptions used to estimate the cost of constructing a comparable new source for the >50% reconstruction test.

Identification and cost separation of passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics (list items and costs) to exclude them from the reconstruction cost calculation per § 63.9290(a)(3).

Identification and cost separation of air pollution control equipment and any retrofits or replacements installed specifically to comply with this NESHAP (exclude these costs from reconstruction calculation per § 63.826(c)).
Identification of any minor ancillary equipment replaced (e.g., piping, ductwork, valves) and inclusion of those replacement costs in the reconstruction cost calculation per § 63.2.

Records or evidence showing whether replacements/additions were planned/contracted as part of a single continuous program (contracts, multi-phase project schedules, board approvals) to evaluate the 'commenced' element in § 63.2.

If reconstruction is plausible, documentation assessing technological and economic feasibility of meeting the relevant new-source standards (technical capability and cost/benefit evidence) as required by the reconstruction definition in § 63.2.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Halogenated Solvent Cleaning Machines (Subpart T)

criteria.criterion: If an individual batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine uses any listed halogenated HAP solvent (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform) in a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent, then that machine is subject to Subpart T.

If a device only performs wipe cleaning (e.g., rags, small spray cleaners) or a solvent cleaning machine does not use any of the listed halogenated HAP solvents above 5 percent by weight, then that activity or machine is not subject to Subpart T.

If you are an owner or operator of a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that is complying with the standards in § 63.463, then you must submit an annual report (by February 1 for the prior calendar year) including the training statement and an estimate of solvent consumption.

If your facility qualifies as an affected facility under § 63.471 (i.e., all solvent cleaning machines at a major source or the applicable set at an area source that are subject to the facility-wide limits), then the owner/operator must submit a solvent emission report every year documenting average monthly consumption and 12-month rolling totals.

If a cleaning machine has been removed or converted so it no longer uses halogenated HAP solvents, then you must retain a record on site documenting the applicability determination (i.e., that the machine no longer uses regulated halogenated solvents) for the period specified by the General Provisions as applied to Subpart T.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) — applicability as applied to Subpart T

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator has a solvent cleaning machine meeting the applicability criteria of § 63.460(a), then the General Provisions in Subpart A apply to that owner/operator except as specifically modified by Subpart T (see Appendix B to Subpart T for which Subpart A sections apply or are excluded).

checklist: Inventory every cleaning device on site and classify each as: batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, batch cold, or only wipe cleaning.

For each cleaning machine, confirm whether any of these halogenated HAP solvents are present in the solvent formulation: methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform.
For any solvent containing suspect HAP(s), determine the total concentration (%) by weight of the listed halogenated HAPs using EPA Method 18, MSDS information, or engineering calculations.
For each machine with halogenated HAPs >5% by weight, document machine location, machine type, solvent/air interface area or cleaning capacity, and annual solvent consumption.

If all machines have been removed or converted, assemble and retain an on-site written record showing the applicability determination (that machines were removed/converted and no longer use listed halogenated HAP solvents) and the date of that change; ensure this record is kept for the period required by Subpart T as applied to Subpart A (see Appendix B/63.1(b)(3)).

Determine whether the facility is an 'affected facility' for § 63.471 purposes (are you a major source and/or do you have units subject to the facility-wide limits) and, if so, maintain monthly solvent addition/removal records to calculate 12-month rolling totals.

If any batch vapor or in-line machine remains subject and complies under § 63.463, verify whether annual reporting under § 63.468(f) is required and prepare the required training statement and solvent consumption estimates.
Check historical reporting: note dates of any initial notifications, compliance statements, or most recent annual/solvent emission reports previously submitted under Subpart T.

candidates.title: Organic Liquids Distribution (Non-Gasoline) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an organic liquids distribution (OLD) operation located at, or part of, a major source of HAP, then that OLD operation is subject to Subpart EEEE.

If transfer racks at which organic liquids are loaded into or unloaded out of transport vehicles and/or containers are present at the site, then those transfer racks are part of the affected source for this subpart.

If the liquid being transferred contains 5 percent by weight or greater of the organic HAP listed in Table 1 to this subpart (i.e., is an "organic liquid"), then the transfer and storage of that liquid fall within the OLD definitions for this subpart.

If the collection of transfer racks at the facility meets the total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume criterion for control in Table 2 (items 7–10), then those transfer racks must comply with the control and operating requirements of § 63.2346 for transfer racks.
citations: 40 CFR 63.2406 ("Total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume")

criteria.criterion: If storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are part of an affected source under another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP, then those items are excluded from the OLD affected source under this subpart.

If transfer racks, storage tanks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are non-permanent and are used only in special situation distribution loading/unloading operations (such as maintenance or upset liquids management), then they are not part of the affected source for this subpart.

candidates.title: Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a vegetable oil production process that is a major source of HAP emissions (or is collocated on a plant site that is a major source) and the process processes any of the listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower), then the process is an affected source subject to Subpart GGGG.
If the vegetable oil production process uses only mechanical extraction techniques that use no organic solvent to remove oil from a listed oilseed, then the process is not subject to Subpart GGGG.
If the vegetable oil production process uses only batch solvent extraction and batch desolventizing equipment, then the process is not subject to Subpart GGGG.

If the process removes oil from listed oilseeds by direct contact with an organic solvent (for example, a hexane isomer blend), then it meets the definition of a solvent extraction vegetable oil production process and is subject to the subpart if the major-source and oilseed criteria are met.

If you exclusively use a solvent where the volume fraction of each HAP is 1 percent or less by volume in each delivery (low-HAP solvent), then you must follow the low-HAP solvent option and the source is not subject to the requirements in §§ 63.2850 through 63.2870 except as specifically referenced.
If the facility functions only as a research and development facility and is not a major source, then it is not subject to Subpart GGGG.

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined).
Confirm whether the facility operates an organic liquids distribution (OLD) operation (storage, transfer, transfer racks, loading/unloading of liquids to/from transport vehicles).
Confirm whether the solvent being handled (hexane) meets the subpart's definition of an "organic liquid" (contains ≥5% by weight of organic HAP listed in Table 1 to Subpart EEEE).
For transfer racks, calculate the facility-level total actual annual organic liquid loading volume (3-year rolling average) and compare to Table 2 control thresholds referenced in § 63.2346(b).
Verify whether the transfer racks and transport equipment are permanent/routine or are non-permanent used only for special situation (maintenance/upset) operations.
Verify whether the specific storage tanks/transfer racks/transport vehicles/equipment leak components are already part of an affected source covered under another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP.
If a vegetable oil production process exists: confirm whether it is solvent extraction (direct contact with organic solvent such as hexane) or mechanical/batch extraction.

If solvent extraction: confirm which oilseeds are processed and whether any listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower) are processed and the tonnage (for applicability and solvent-loss factors).

If considering the low-HAP solvent option for the vegetable oil process: obtain documentation for each solvent delivery showing each HAP is ≤1% by volume and maintain delivery records per § 63.2840(e).

For transport vehicles and unloading operations: verify vapor-collection/vapor-tight status and U.S. DOT certifications or Method 27 test records as applicable per Subpart EEEE recordkeeping requirements.

Determine whether the solvent unloading racks and transport equipment are dedicated to the vegetable oil production process or are part of facility-wide OLD distribution activities (affects which subpart's criteria apply).

candidates.title: NESHAP for Polymers and Resins (Subpart JJJ)

criteria.criterion: If a process unit is designated as a thermoplastic product process unit (TPPU) at a plant site that is a major source and the pressure relief devices are in organic HAP service, then the pressure relief device provisions of this subpart apply to those devices.

If a pressure relief device in organic HAP service is designed and operated to route all pressure releases through a closed vent system to a control device, process, or drain system, then the pressure relief device operating, monitoring, and pressure release management requirements in §63.1331(a)(9)(i)-(iii) do not apply to that device.

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: If equipment (including pressure relief devices) is intended to operate in organic HAP service 300 hours or more during the calendar year within a source subject to a specific subpart that references this subpart, then the pressure relief device standards in §63.165 apply.

If a pressure relief device is routed to a process or fuel gas system or equipped with a closed-vent system capable of capturing and transporting all releases to a control device or process, then the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of §63.165 do not apply to that device.

candidates.title: HON Equipment Leak and Transfer Rack Provisions (Subpart PPP)

criteria.criterion: If the source is an affected source as described in §63.1420(a) (i.e., subject to Subpart PPP) and a pressure relief device is in organic HAP service, then the pressure relief device operating, monitoring, and pressure release management requirements in §63.1434(c) apply to that device.

If a pressure relief device in organic HAP service is designed and operated to route all pressure releases through a closed vent system to a control device, process, or drain system, then the owner or operator is not required to comply with the operating, monitoring, and pressure release management paragraphs of §63.1434(c) for that device.

candidates.title: Pressure Relief Device Requirements (Subpart OOO)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator is subject to Subpart OOO and a pressure relief device is in organic HAP gas or vapor service, then the device must be operated, monitored after a pressure release, and managed in accordance with §63.1411(a)–(c).

If a pressure relief device is designed and operated to route all HAP emissions from pressure releases through a closed vent system to a control device or to a process, fuel gas system, or drain system, then the requirements of §63.1411(a), (b), and (c) do not apply to that device.

checklist: Is the plant a major source for HAPs (determine major source status for the plant site)?
Is the process unit(s) producing a thermoplastic product and designated as a TPPU under §63.1310 (i.e., does the primary product meet the TPPU criteria)?

Are the portable containers and their pressure relief devices operating in organic HAP service (verify composition/percent organic HAP of the fluid contacting the container and frequency/duration of service)?

For each pressure relief device: is it routed to a closed vent system and control device, routed to a process or fuel gas system, or to a drain system (if yes, many PRD requirements may be inapplicable)?

For each pressure relief device: does it include or consist of a rupture disk, is it pilot-operated, on mobile equipment, or in heavy-liquid service (these affect which requirements/exemptions apply)?
How many hours per calendar year does each device operate in organic HAP service (is it >= 300 hours for applicability under §63.160)?
Are the devices located on containers that meet any storage-vessel exclusions (e.g., capacity, mobile equipment, pressure-rated vessels) that would change applicability under Subpart JJJ definitions?

For an alternative monitoring plan: which specific Subpart(s) (JJJ, H, PPP, OOO) the facility is claiming applicability under (document the affected-source designation and reference the applicable subpart notification/assignment)?

If a pressure release has occurred or could occur: are procedures and capabilities in place to detect/releases (rupture-disk indicators, stem motion sensors, flow/pressure monitors), record time/duration, calculate HAP quantity released, and perform root-cause/corrective-action analyses within required timeframes?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Pulp and Paper Industry (Subpart S)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator is subject to the standards in §§ 63.443(c) and (d), 63.444(b) and (c), 63.445(b) and (c), 63.446(c), (d), and (e), 63.447(b), or § 63.450(d) then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system (CMS) with a continuous recorder as specified in § 63.453(a).

If the owner or operator uses a control device, technique, or an alternative parameter other than those specified in paragraphs (b) through (l) of § 63.453 then the owner or operator must install a CMS and establish appropriate operating parameters to be monitored to demonstrate continuous compliance to the Administrator's satisfaction as required by § 63.453(m).

If the owner or operator seeks to establish or reestablish monitoring parameter values or site-specific monitored parameters required under paragraphs (b) through (j), (l), and (m) of § 63.453 or for parameters in paragraphs (f), (i), (j)(2), and (m), then the owner or operator must use the procedures in § 63.453(n)(1)–(4) and provide the rationale and data to the Administrator for approval.

If the owner or operator is required to perform initial or repeat performance tests for emission sources subject to §§ 63.443–63.447 then the owner or operator must conduct the performance tests and use the test methods and procedures in § 63.457 to develop monitoring parameters and demonstrate compliance as required by § 63.457(a).

If the owner or operator proposes to use an alternative test or analytical method to measure total HAP or methanol concentrations (instead of the listed methods), then any such method must be demonstrated to and accepted by the Administrator as allowed in §§ 63.457(b)(5)(iii) and 63.457(c)(3)(iii).

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements for kraft/soda recovery furnaces and lime kilns (Subpart MM)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator operates an affected kraft or soda recovery furnace or lime kiln equipped with an ESP then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) in accordance with PS-1 and the provisions of § 63.864(d).

If the owner or operator has a kraft or soda recovery furnace or lime kiln using an ESP followed by a wet scrubber then the owner or operator must comply with the CPMS requirements for wet scrubbers (pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow rate) in § 63.864(e)(10) and may omit the COMS per § 63.864(e)(2).

If the owner or operator uses an air pollution control system other than an ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, or fabric filter, or seeks to monitor alternative control device parameters, then the owner or operator must submit an alternative monitoring request to the Administrator including a description of the control device, test results verifying performance, operating parameters to be monitored, how limits are set, frequency of measurement, and proposed performance specifications and QA procedures as required by § 63.864(e)(14).

If the owner or operator establishes operating limits for CPMS or CPMS-based parameters then those operating limits must be determined during initial or periodic performance testing as specified in § 63.864(j) and (j)(1)–(5).

candidates.title: Alternative compliance requirements procedures (Subpart QQQQQ)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator uses a control technique other than a solvent recovery system and/or solvent substitution and seeks to use an alternative method to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations then the owner or operator may request approval of an alternative method according to § 63.9570(a) and (b).

If the owner or operator requests approval to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance then the owner or operator must submit a description of the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting and the proposed basis for demonstrating compliance, including a monitoring plan and, if no prior testing, a proposed test plan as required in § 63.9570(c).

If the owner or operator submits an alternative compliance proposal based on previously performed testing then the submission must include results of testing, procedures followed, and pertinent testing conditions per § 63.9570(c)(1).

If the Administrator approves the alternative method, then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, operate, and maintain monitors in accordance with the approved monitoring plan before using the alternative method as required in § 63.9570(c) and (d).

candidates.title: How to apply for alternative monitoring requirements for a continuous emissions monitoring system (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator wishes to request an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance with applicable VOHAP emissions limits (or other CEMS-like requirements), then the owner or operator must submit a monitoring plan containing the control technique description, a description of the continuous monitoring system or method and operating parameters, test results demonstrating compliance, operating limit(s), frequency of measurement and recording, and O&M requirements as specified in § 63.7747(c).

If the owner or operator submits an alternative monitoring plan then the monitoring plan is subject to the Administrator's approval and the use of the alternative monitoring method must not begin until approval is granted as required by § 63.7747(d).

checklist: Confirm the facility and specific equipment are a kraft pulping system subject to Subpart S (identify which §§63.443–63.447 provisions apply to your equipment: e.g., brownstock washer vents, oxygen delignification, bleach system, pulping process condensates, steam strippers, biological treatment).

List all control devices and treatment systems for HAPs (e.g., thermal oxidizer/RTO, wet scrubber, steam stripper, open biological units, closed-vent condensate collection, recovery furnace/ESP) and note which devices match the parameter-monitoring items enumerated in 40 CFR 63.453(b)–(l).

Determine whether you plan to use monitoring parameters or a control technique that differ from the parameters specified in § 63.453(b)–(l); if so, plan to submit an alternative monitoring/CMS proposal to the Administrator per § 63.453(m) and § 63.453(n).

Identify which performance tests have been or will be conducted for the affected emission sources (initial and periodic), and ensure tests follow § 63.457(a) and the test methods/procedures in § 63.457 (select methods for methanol, total HAP, chlorine, etc.).

Decide the HAP measurement approach (sum of individual HAPs vs. methanol surrogate) and the test method (e.g., Method 305 adjustment, NCASI DI/MEOH-94.03, Method 308, ASTM D6348-03) as allowed in § 63.457 and document method-specific requirements.

If recovery furnace/lim e kiln present, confirm whether an ESP and/or wet scrubber are installed and whether COMS or CPMS requirements of Subpart MM apply (install COMS per § 63.864(d) or CPMS per § 63.864(e)(10) as applicable).

Prepare an alternative monitoring plan that at minimum includes: description of control/treatment technique, description of proposed monitoring method(s) and operating parameters, test results verifying performance, operating limit(s) and how set, monitoring frequency and averaging time, and QA/QC procedures (per § 63.7747(c), § 63.9570(c), § 63.864(e)(14), and § 63.453(n)(4)).

Collect and assemble data used to set proposed operating limits (performance test records, continuous parameter records during tests, manufacturer recommendations, engineering assessments) as required by § 63.453(n) and the alternative-monitoring procedures in other cited sections.

Verify monitoring instrumentation accuracy and certification requirements that may apply (e.g., CPMS accuracy for scrubber pressure drop and flow in § 63.864(e)(10); method-specific QA requirements in § 63.457(c)(5)(ii) and § 63.457(c)(6)).

Confirm the schedule: submit the alternative monitoring request/plan to the Administrator and do not implement the alternative monitoring until the Administrator approves the plan (see § 63.7747(d), § 63.9570(d), and § 63.1350(o)(2) for analogous timing requirements).

For biological treatment of condensates, verify monitoring and performance test frequency and sample storage requirements (daily monitoring, quarterly performance tests, archival sample storage at 4 °C) as specified in § 63.453(j) and § 63.457(n).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Phosphate Fertilizer Production Plants (Subpart BB)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a phosphate fertilizer production plant that is a major source as defined in §63.2, then you are subject to the requirements of Subpart BB for each phosphate fertilizer process line, granular triple superphosphate process line, and granular triple superphosphate storage building at the plant.
If the phosphate fertilizer production plant is an area source as defined in §63.2, then the requirements of Subpart BB do not apply to the plant.

If you use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) to demonstrate compliance with any applicable emission limit, then you must develop and have (and submit to the Administrator upon request) a site-specific monitoring plan that contains the required probe location justification, performance/equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, O&M procedures, Q/A procedures, recordkeeping/reporting procedures, and a schedule for performance evaluations.
If you use a CMS, then you must conduct CMS performance evaluations consistent with your site-specific monitoring plan and the CMS performance evaluation requirements referenced in this subpart.

If you use a control device to meet an emission limit and monitor operating parameters for that device, then (except where an alternative is specified) you must establish the operating-parameter limit as the arithmetic average of measurements recorded during the three test runs of the most recent performance test (with special alternative procedures for absorber pressure drop described in the rule).

If you install a bag leak detection system to comply with the fabric filter requirements in this subpart, then you must include in the site-specific monitoring plan the bag leak performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria and a corrective action plan as specified in §63.628(d).

If a bag leak detection alarm on a required bag leak detection system is triggered, then you must identify the cause within 1 hour and initiate corrective action no later than 48 hours after the alarm (failure to do so is a violation).

If you propose alternative monitoring parameters under §63.8(f) (petitioned alternatives), then the site-specific monitoring plan requirements of §63.628(c) apply and must reflect those petitioned alternatives.

If you must perform initial and subsequent performance tests for emission limits, then you must conduct an initial performance test within 180 days of the applicable compliance date and thereafter at least once per calendar year (subject to restart provisions).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A of Part 63) as made applicable to Subpart BB

criteria.criterion: If Subpart BB applies to your source, then the monitoring and alternative monitoring provisions in Subpart A (including the CMS requirements and the alternative monitoring provisions) apply to Subpart BB as indicated in Appendix A to Subpart BB.
If you use a CMS to demonstrate compliance, then the CMS performance evaluation requirements in Subpart A (including §63.8(e)) apply to your CMS performance evaluations as applicable to Subpart BB.

If you want to pursue alternative monitoring methods, then the alternative monitoring method provisions in Subpart A (§63.8(f) paragraphs shown applicable in Appendix A) apply and you must follow the applicable procedures for alternatives.

candidates.title: Extension, waiver, and alternative monitoring approval procedures (Subpart YY)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance with a relevant standard, then you must submit a written application to the Administrator not later than with the site-specific test plan or at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin (or with the site-specific performance evaluation plan if requested).

If you submit an application to use an alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator will notify you of approval or intention to deny within 30 days after receipt of the original request and within 30 days after receipt of any supplementary information submitted.

If the Administrator approves the use of an alternative monitoring method for an affected source, then you must continue to use the approved alternative monitoring method until the Administrator approves use of another monitoring method.

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source or an area source under 40 CFR 63.2.

Identify which affected sources at the plant are subject to Subpart BB (each phosphate fertilizer process line, granular triple superphosphate process line, and granular triple superphosphate storage building per 40 CFR 63.620(b)).

Confirm whether you use a CMS to demonstrate compliance and, if so, locate your current site-specific monitoring plan and note the date it was submitted or whether it has been submitted upon request (see 40 CFR 63.628(c)).
Verify the dates of your initial and most recent annual performance tests and the scheduled date(s) for the next required performance test(s) per 40 CFR 63.626(a)–(c).

If you plan to change the timing of CMS performance evaluations (e.g., conduct evaluations within a 5-day window prior to a performance test), confirm whether you will be using the alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance and prepare to submit an application to the Administrator at least 60 days before the performance evaluation (or with the site-specific test plan) per 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4)(i).

Check whether any control device operating-parameter limits were established from the arithmetic average of three test runs and whether your proposed evaluation timing would affect establishing or demonstrating those parameter averages (see 40 CFR 63.625(d)(1)(i)).

If you have fabric filters with bag leak detectors, confirm the bag leak detection system details and that your site-specific monitoring plan includes the performance evaluation procedures, acceptance criteria, and corrective action plan per 40 CFR 63.628(d) and that alarm-response timing requirements in 40 CFR 63.625(e)(9) can be met.

Document whether any petition under §63.8(f) or other alternative monitoring requests have been submitted previously and whether Administrator approval has been granted or is required (see 40 CFR 63.628(c) and 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4)–(5)).

Prepare evidence and schedules to support the alternative-monitoring application (justification, performance-evaluation test plan, and any technical/economic infeasibility rationale) so it can be submitted in accordance with 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4)(ii).

Confirm you can meet the submission and response timeframes (submit at least 60 days prior; expect Administrator response within 30 days after original or supplemental submissions) and be ready to continue using the approved method until further notice (see 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4)(i) and 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(5)(i),(iii)).

candidates.title: NESHAP for Catalytic Cracking Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: If your catalytic cracking unit regenerator is subject to this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain continuous monitoring systems and establish site-specific operating limits and an operation, maintenance, and monitoring plan as required by this subpart.

If a specific control device (for example a wet scrubber) may be monitored using more than one continuous parameter monitoring system, then you may select which parameter to use for compliance but you must notify the Administrator (or designated authority) if you elect to change the monitoring option.

If you want to adopt alternative monitoring parameters (including adjusting parametric operating limits) for demonstrating continuous compliance, then you must submit a request with the required demonstration information and obtain Administrator approval under the alternative-monitoring procedures in this subpart.

If your FCCU uses a wet scrubber and the regenerator vent is subject to the PM NSPS and you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring under the NSPS, then you may request alternative monitoring requirements under this subpart for that same regenerator vent consistent with § 63.1573(g).

If you conducted a performance test to demonstrate compliance, then the continuous-parameter operating limits must be based on the results of that performance test, subject to the specific adjustment rules in this section (including limited allowance to adjust one monitored parameter to a worst-case representative value with supporting documentation).

If you wish to change an established operating limit for a continuous parameter monitoring system, then you must perform an additional performance test, a performance test with an engineering assessment, or an engineering assessment to verify compliance at the new operating limit before establishing the revised limit.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under the referencing subpart, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate CPMS equipment according to the manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures providing adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and you must establish a range for monitored parameters indicating proper operation of the control device.

If you seek to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring or to monitor a different parameter than those established, then you may request Administrator approval of alternatives as provided in this section and the referencing subpart.

candidates.title: Change of compliance levels for monitored parameters (Subpart DDD)

criteria.criterion: If you want to expand the range of a control device or process operating parameter level that was established during performance tests, then you must notify the Administrator of the desire to expand the range and, upon Administrator approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels and verify compliance with the applicable emission limits before operating at those new levels.

candidates.title: NESHAP monitoring requirements for control devices (Subpart OOO)

criteria.criterion: If a scrubber is used to comply with this subpart, then you must install a continuous pH recorder for scrubber effluent and a continuous liquid-flow measurement device at the scrubber influent and determine gas-stream flow using one of the specified methods.

If you want to monitor parameters other than those specified in Table 3 of this subpart for a control device, then you must request approval for alternative monitoring parameters according to the procedures specified in this subpart.

If organic HAP emissions are vented to a control device subject to this subpart, then required monitoring equipment must be in operation at all times when those emissions are vented to the control device.

checklist: Confirm that the FCCU catalyst regenerator vent is subject to Subpart UUU (i.e., the unit is an affected catalytic cracking unit and subject to 40 CFR part 63 requirements).
Confirm whether the FCCU regenerator vent is also subject to the PM NSPS (40 CFR 60.102) and whether you have Administrator‑approved alternative monitoring under 40 CFR 60.105(a)(1).

Confirm the type of control device on the FCCU regenerator (wet scrubber) and which monitored parameters are currently used for compliance (e.g., pressure drop, liquid-to-gas ratio, scrubber effluent pH, liquid flow, opacity, CO, O2, gas flow).

Determine whether the wet scrubber is subject to any other subpart operating limits for pressure drop or liquid flow (e.g., whether § 63.9890(b) or similar applies) that would require CPMS monitoring of hourly averages.
Verify whether you have completed the required initial performance test(s) for the FCCU regenerator and have established the site-specific operating limits based on those test results.

If you plan to change operating limits or expand parameter ranges, determine whether you will conduct an additional performance test or engineering assessment and prepare supporting documentation as required by § 63.1571(e) and § 63.1571(d).

Prepare or update the operation, maintenance, and monitoring (OMM) plan to include the proposed alternative monitored parameters, the rationale/demonstration showing the parameter indicates proper operation, monitoring frequency, averaging time, and quality control procedures per § 63.1574(f).

Determine whether Administrator approval (or permitting authority review) is required and plan to submit the formal request for alternative monitoring with supporting calculations, test results, and the monitoring plan per § 63.1573(f) and § 63.1573(g).

Verify that continuous parameter monitoring systems meet the installation, operation, calibration, data-recording, and data-availability requirements in § 63.1572 (cycle times, valid-data percentage, recordkeeping) and in Subpart SS general monitoring requirements.

Confirm who (EPA or delegated permitting authority) is the decisionmaker for approving monitoring changes and include required notifications (Notification of Compliance Status) and supporting information when submitting changes as required by § 63.1574.

candidates.title: Continuous monitoring requirements for control devices for process vents (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and the control device is subject to CPMS requirements in §63.11925(c), then you must install pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet to monitor the pressure drop through the absorber or acid gas scrubber.

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring parameter or procedure in place of the continuous operating parameters listed in this section (for example, substituting ambient pressure for the measured outlet pressure), then you may request approval to use alternatives as specified in this subpart and the approval procedures in the notification/permit provisions.

If a CPMS is required for a control device, then the CPMS must provide continuous records at least once every 15 minutes and meet the equipment range/resolution requirements specified for CPMS in this subpart.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then the general monitoring conduct, installation, O&M, and QA/QC requirements in §63.996 apply to your control device monitoring.

If you seek to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring or to monitor a different parameter than those established under the referencing subpart, then you may request Administrator approval as provided in §63.996(d)(1) and §63.996(d)(2).

If a CPMS is used as a backup to another CPMS then you must report results from the CPMS used to meet the monitoring requirements and follow the reporting rules for periods where each instrument was relied upon.

candidates.title: Process vent provisions—monitoring requirements (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If your process vent uses a scrubber with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater for halogenated vent streams to comply with the process vent requirements, then you must install a pH monitoring device and a flow meter at the scrubber influent for liquid flow and determine gas flow by one of the specified procedures (including design blower capacity adjusted for pressure drop).

If you use one of the combustion or recovery/recapture devices listed in this section but seek to monitor a parameter other than those specified, then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the procedures in this subpart.

If a bypass line could divert a gas stream to atmosphere, then you must either install a flow indicator at the entrance to the bypass line that takes readings at least once every 15 minutes or secure the bypass valve and visually inspect it at least monthly.

candidates.title: Monitoring and inspection requirements for affected sources (Subpart MMM)

criteria.criterion: If you are using a liquid scrubber to control HAP under this subpart, then you must establish a minimum scrubber liquid flow rate or pressure drop as a site-specific operating parameter and measure and record that parameter at least once every 15 minutes during periods the scrubber controls HAP.

If you wish to request approval to monitor parameters other than those specified for control devices under this subpart, then you may request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the procedures specified in this section.

If monitoring devices are used to determine pressure drop, then the monitoring device used to determine the pressure drop must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within a gauge pressure of ±10 percent of the maximum pressure drop measured and must be calibrated annually (where applicable).

checklist: Is this facility an affected polyvinyl chloride production unit subject to Subpart HHHHHHH (i.e., are the process vents and control devices regulated under Table 1 or 2 of Subpart HHHHHHH)?

Is the control device for the second scrubber an absorber or acid gas scrubber used to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 of Subpart HHHHHHH (or otherwise a scrubber covered by Subpart G/MMM/other applicable subpart)?
Is CPMS/CEMS required for this scrubber under §63.11925(c) (or equivalent requirement in the applicable subpart)?

Are inlet and outlet pressure gauges currently installed on the scrubber and do they record continuous data at least once every 15 minutes (or would the proposed ambient-pressure substitution produce equivalent continuous records)?

What exact parameter do you propose to monitor (ambient pressure at what location) and what engineering rationale/data show ambient pressure is representative for calculating pressure drop across the scrubber under all operating scenarios?

What are the normal and expected operating ranges for inlet pressure and outlet pressure so you can demonstrate the proposed monitor meets the CPMS required measurement range (at least 20% beyond normal per §63.11935(c)(6))?

Does the proposed ambient-pressure instrument meet the accuracy and resolution requirements (e.g., pressure gauge certified to ±10% of maximum pressure drop per §63.1366(b)(1)(ii)(A), CPMS resolution equal to or better than one-half required system accuracy per §63.11935(c)(6)) and annual calibration frequency where required?

Have you prepared or can you prepare a site-specific monitoring plan (performance criteria, sampling location, QA/QC, data collection, and rationale for operating limits) as required by §63.11935(c)(1) and the alternative-monitoring request requirements in §63.11985(c)(4)-(5)?

Was the prior approval you received for the other scrubber documented (approval letter, conditions, scope, date)? Obtain the approval documentation and confirm whether its scope and conditions match the current proposed substitution.

Are you submitting the alternative-monitoring request at the appropriate time relative to your Notification of Compliance Status or permit application (note §63.11985(c)(4) and (c)(5) reference timing and required content)?
Who is the approving 'Administrator' for your source (EPA Region or delegated Texas agency)? Confirm the correct recipient and whether the delegation affects the approval pathway.

Can you identify and assemble test data or engineering analyses showing the operating limit(s) that will demonstrate the control device meets emission limits when monitored using the proposed ambient-pressure parameter (to be included with the monitoring plan or alternative request)?
Will monitoring records be continuous and reducible to the averaging periods required by the applicable subpart (e.g., 15-minute CPMS records and 1-hour average reductions per §63.11935(e))?

If there are bypass lines, is the bypass monitoring/lock/seal approach compliant with the applicable subpart's bypass-line monitoring requirements (e.g., flow indicator readings at least once every 15 minutes or secured valve plus monthly inspections)?

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLLL

criteria.criterion: If you operate polymerization process equipment or monomer recovery process equipment that emits acrylonitrile (AN), then you must collect those gases in capture/enclosure systems and convey them through a closed vent to a control device.

If you use a wet scrubber to control polymerization process equipment, then you must maintain a daily average water flow rate of at least 50 liters per minute and operate a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) that records the water flow at least every 15 minutes.

If you use a wet scrubber to control monomer recovery process equipment, then you must maintain a daily average water flow rate of at least 30 liters per minute and operate a CPMS that records the water flow at least every 15 minutes.

If you do not use a wet scrubber for the polymerization or monomer recovery process equipment, then you must submit a monitoring plan to the Administrator containing a device description, performance test results per § 63.1104 of subpart YY, an O&M plan and continuous monitoring description, list of monitored operating parameters, and operating parameter limits based on performance test data.

If you want to change the wet scrubber operating limits, then you must notify the Administrator to conduct a new performance test, conduct the test to demonstrate compliance, and establish revised operating limits using CPMS data from the test runs.

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then § 63.996 applies and you must conduct monitoring as set forth in this section and in the relevant referencing subpart.
If the Administrator specifies or approves minor changes or approves alternatives, then you may deviate from the specified monitoring methodologies or procedures in this subpart.

If you operate CPMS, then the equipment must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to the manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and be operated consistent with good air pollution control practices.

candidates.title: Subpart PPP

criteria.criterion: If you use an absorber or wet scrubber to comply with the process vent control requirements in this subpart, then you must install and operate a scrubbing liquid flow rate meter or a pressure monitoring device (each with a continuous recorder) and, if an acid or base absorbent is used, a pH monitoring device for the scrubber effluent.

If you wish to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubbers in this section, then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters and follow the submission procedures specified in the process vent reporting and alternative-parameter sections referenced in this subpart.

If you vent emissions through a closed vent system to adsorbers regenerated offsite or nonregenerative adsorbers, then you must install two or more adsorber units in series and follow the monitoring and breakthrough procedures specified in this section.

candidates.title: Subpart UUU

criteria.criterion: If you operate a wet scrubber that is a jet ejector type or other scrubber equipped with atomizing spray nozzles, then you may use the alternative to continuous pressure-drop monitoring consisting of a daily check of the air or water pressure to the spray nozzles, record the results, and repair or replace faulty lines within 12 hours of identification.

If you operate a catalytic reforming unit and want an alternative to continuous pH or alkalinity monitoring of the wet scrubber, then you may use hourly pH strips or hourly alkalinity titration during coke burn-off and rejuvenation cycles as specified.

If you want to use an alternative monitoring parameter or method not specified in the applicable subpart, then you must submit a written request to the Administrator that includes a description of the affected source and parameter(s), methods and demonstration procedures, monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and the averaging time for the alternative parameter.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility and specific emission points (polymerization process equipment and/or monomer recovery) are subject sources under Subpart LLLLLL (i.e., PAN/polymerization with acrylonitrile).
Identify which emission streams are routed to your scrubber(s) and whether those scrubbers are used to control polymerization process equipment or monomer recovery process equipment.
Verify scrubber type (wet scrubber, jet-ejector, absorber, acid/base scrubbing reagent) and whether the scrubbing liquid is acidic/basic (triggers pH monitoring requirements).
Determine whether the scrubber already has a CPMS or continuous recorder measuring liquid flow and whether it records at least once every 15 minutes as required by 63.11395(e).
Determine current daily average water flow rates to each scrubber (calculate whether they meet ≥50 l/min for polymerization control and ≥30 l/min for monomer recovery control under 63.11395(c)).

Assemble recent performance test data for the control device (AN emission performance tests) to support any alternative monitoring request or to establish/justify operating limits per 63.11395(h),(k).

If proposing alternative monitoring, prepare the application materials identified in 63.1573(f): description of source and parameter(s), demonstration methods and schedule, monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and averaging time.
If proposing the jet-ejector pressure alternative, confirm daily check procedures, recordkeeping practice, and repair response (repair within 12 hours) to meet 63.1573(b).

If proposing pH strip or titration alternative for catalytic reforming scrubbers, verify ability to perform hourly measurements during required cycles and that pH strips meet any referenced acceptance criteria (63.1573(c)).
Confirm O&M procedures and that monitoring equipment will be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated per manufacturer specifications and good air pollution control practices per 63.996(c).
Confirm whether bypass lines exist and whether flow indicators or secured valves are required per the applicable process-vent subpart monitoring provisions (e.g., 63.1429(c), 63.11395 requirements).

Plan to submit any alternative-monitoring request to the Administrator well in advance of performance testing or compliance deadlines, and be prepared for the Administrator to approve, deny, or require additional information as described in 63.1573(e) and 63.996(d).
