candidates.title: Subpart RRRRR

criteria.criterion: If you apply a dynamic wet scrubber to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and either the daily average fan amperage (a surrogate for fan speed) or the daily average pressure drop at or above the minimum levels established during the initial performance test.

If a dynamic wet scrubber is subject to performance testing, then you must establish site-specific operating limits by measuring and recording scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test and set the operating limits as the lowest average values corresponding to any of the three test runs.

If you operate a dynamic wet scrubber subject to these operating limits, then you must install, operate, and maintain a CPMS and monitor the daily average scrubber water flow rate and either the daily average fan amperage or daily average pressure drop according to the monitoring requirements.

If the daily average scrubber water flow rate or daily average fan amperage (or pressure drop) is below the operating limits established for the unit, then you must follow the corrective action procedures required for dynamic wet scrubbers and report deviations as specified.

If you must demonstrate initial compliance for a dynamic wet scrubber, then you must have a record of the scrubber water flow rate and either the fan amperage or pressure drop values measured during the performance test in accordance with the required procedures.

candidates.title: Subpart TTTTT

criteria.criterion: If you apply a wet scrubber to meet any particulate matter, PM10, chlorine, hydrochloric acid, or dioxins/furans emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must maintain the hourly average pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate at or above the minimum level established during the initial or subsequent performance test.

If a wet scrubber is subject to performance testing under this subpart, then you must establish site-specific operating limits by using a CPMS to measure and record pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes during each run and set operating limits as the lowest average individual pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate values in any of the three runs that meet the emission limit.

candidates.title: Subpart DDD

criteria.criterion: If you want to change (expand) the control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests, then you must notify the Administrator and, upon approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels to verify compliance with the applicable emission limits before operating at those levels.

candidates.title: Subpart MM

criteria.criterion: If your affected source is a kraft or soda recovery furnace, kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank, kraft or soda lime kiln, or sulfite combustion unit equipped with a dynamic wet scrubber under this subpart, then you may use fan amperage or fan RPM as an alternative to pressure drop monitoring for applicable dynamic scrubbers and may set the minimum percent full load amperage (PFLA) operating limit as the percent of full load amperage under no-load plus 10 percent when establishing limits during performance testing.

If you wish to monitor alternative control device operating parameters (other than the standard parameters in this subpart), then you must obtain prior written approval by the Administrator and include how the parameter operating limit is to be set.

checklist: Confirm whether each scrubber at your facility is a "dynamic wet scrubber" as defined (mechanically powered fan causing contact between exhaust and scrubbing liquid).

Determine whether each dynamic wet scrubber is used to meet a particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 of Subpart RRRRR (taconite MACT) or is controlled under Subpart TTTTT limits (verify applicable subpart for each emission unit).
Verify the construction/reconstruction date(s) of the affected sources relative to 9/25/2019 and 7/28/2020 to determine which monitoring/establishment timing provisions apply.

Confirm whether initial performance tests have been conducted for each dynamic wet scrubber and whether those tests recorded 15‑minute (or listed) measurements of scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage and/or pressure drop for each test run.
Obtain the test-run average values from the initial performance tests (the lowest average of the three runs is used to set the operating limit under the cited procedures).

Verify whether a CPMS that records the required parameter(s) (fan amperage, pressure drop, and scrubber water flow) at the required frequency (every 15 minutes) is installed, properly calibrated, and maintained.

Decide which parameter averaging period applies to your unit(s): Subpart RRRRR requires daily averages for dynamic scrubbers, while Subpart TTTTT specifies hourly averages—confirm which subpart governs each unit.

If you intend to set a PFLA-based minimum (percent full load amperage = no-load percent + 10%), obtain manufacturer no-load amperage specifications or perform a no-load test of each fan motor to determine the no-load amperage.

If you propose an alternate parametric limit (PFLA or other) that differs from the site-specific values established during initial performance testing, prepare to notify and obtain written approval from the Administrator and, if required, conduct additional performance testing before operating at the new levels.

Confirm that monitoring data collection, averaging, and retention meet the CPMS and compliance recordkeeping requirements (e.g., daily averages, corrective action logs) specified in the applicable subpart.

If an operating parameter drops below its established operating limit, be prepared to follow the corrective action schedule (initiate corrective action within 10 calendar days and document results) and report deviations as required.

If you claim applicability of the Subpart MM provision allowing PFLA = no-load percent + 10%, verify that your source type (kraft/soda smelt dissolving tank, lime kiln, etc.) is covered by Subpart MM; if not covered, you must rely on RRRRR/TTTTT procedures or obtain Administrator approval for an alternative monitoring approach.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Automobiles and Light-Duty Trucks

criteria.criterion: If a previously conducted transfer efficiency test was performed using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart, then you may use its results in lieu of performing a new transfer efficiency test.

If no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous transfer efficiency test (or you can demonstrate that the previous test results remain reliable despite any process or equipment changes), then you may use the previous test results.

If the required operating parameters were established in the previous test or sufficient data were collected in the previous test to establish the required operating parameters, then you may use the previous test results to define those operating parameters.

If the prior transfer efficiency test was not conducted under representative operating conditions (for the coating operation, emission capture system, and add-on control device) or was conducted during periods of startup, shutdown, malfunction, or SSM that do not constitute representative conditions, then you may not rely on that test as a representative performance test.

If the transfer efficiency determination used one of the approved methods (ASTM D5066-91 or the EPA Protocol for primer-surfacer and topcoat) and, if applicable, tested representative coatings and representative spray booths following the subpart procedures, then the previous transfer efficiency test method meets the subpart's method requirements.

If you cannot produce the required test report(s), raw data, and documentation demonstrating that the prior test met the subpart procedures and established the necessary operating parameters, then you cannot rely on the prior test without obtaining approval and providing the missing documentation.

checklist: Locate and retain the complete test report(s) and raw data from the December 2004 transfer efficiency test (panel weights, wet/baked weights, calculations, etc.).
Verify which test method was used for the transfer efficiency determination (e.g., ASTM D5066-91 or the EPA Protocol EPA-453/R-08-002) and that the method matches 40 CFR 63.3161(g).

Confirm the test was conducted on representative coatings and representative spray booths (or that representative-coating/booth justification is documented) as required by §63.3161(g) and the Protocol.

Document whether any process or equipment changes (spray equipment, booth geometry, waterwash, curing ovens, line speed, transfer-efficiency-related parameters) have occurred since December 2004; if changes occurred, prepare engineering demonstration or data showing the 2004 results remain reliable per §63.3160(c)(2).

Verify the previous test established the required operating parameters (e.g., transfer efficiency values and any operating limits) or that the test collected sufficient data to derive those parameters as required by §63.3160(c)(3).
Confirm the test was performed under representative operating conditions (not during malfunction, and not during SSM or nonrepresentative conditions) consistent with §63.3164(a)(1).

Check that the test included the necessary number and duration of runs and adhered to the subpart's procedural requirements for transfer efficiency/panel testing (recorded run times, procedures for weighing panels, etc.) as documented in §63.3164 and Appendix A.
Assemble all records required by §63.3130(m) documenting monthly transfer-efficiency calculations, raw data, algorithms, and any conversions used so you can submit/justify reliance on the prior test.

If any required documentation or demonstrations are missing, prepare a plan to either (a) perform a new transfer efficiency test following the cited methods or (b) request Administrator approval to use the prior test results, providing the supporting documentation called for in §63.3160(c) and §63.3161(g).

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter for a control device, then you must install, operate, and maintain a CMS and collect data according to the requirements in 40 CFR 63.9025(a).

If your device is a scrubber used as a control device, then you may request approval from the Administrator under §63.8(f) to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) by submitting a site-specific monitoring plan that identifies the parameter, explains why it is appropriate, and specifies monitoring procedures per 40 CFR 63.9025(b).

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in this subpart, then you must keep records of daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and daily average scrubber effluent pH as specified in 40 CFR 63.9035(b).

candidates.title: Subpart CCC

criteria.criterion: If you are an acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC, then you must conduct performance tests to measure HCl mass flows or outlet concentration at the control device annually or as approved by the permitting authority per 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(1).

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device at an acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate continuously and record at least once per shift while operating per 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(2).

If you wish to use alternative monitoring at a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC, then you may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only with approval by the Administrator per 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(6).

candidates.title: Subpart G

criteria.criterion: If a process vent uses a recovery device or recapture device to comply with §63.113(a)(2), then the owner/operator must install the appropriate monitoring device for the type of recovery device used (e.g., scrubbing liquid temperature and specific gravity where an absorber is the final recovery device) per 40 CFR 63.114(a)(5)(ii) and 40 CFR 63.114(b)(1).

If the owner or operator seeks to monitor parameters other than those specified for process vents and recovery devices in this subpart, then the owner/operator may request approval to monitor other parameters by submitting a request according to the referenced procedures in this subpart per 40 CFR 63.114(c).

If you establish monitored parameters, then you must establish an operating range that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device based on the results of the most recent performance test and submit required information in the Notification of Compliance Status or permit application per 40 CFR 63.114(e).

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under Subpart SS, then the general monitoring requirements in 40 CFR 63.996 apply to your control or recovery device per 40 CFR 63.996(a)(1).

If you seek alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring or to monitor a different parameter than those listed in the subpart-specific monitoring provisions, then you may request Administrator approval to use alternatives or to monitor a different parameter as provided in 40 CFR 63.996(d)(1) and (d)(2) and the cross-referenced procedures.

If you install CPMS/monitoring equipment, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate it according to manufacturer specifications or written procedures and establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation consistent with 40 CFR 63.996(c)(1), (c)(3), and (c)(6).

checklist: Confirm which NESHAP subpart(s) you are expressly subject to (e.g., Subpart CCC, Subpart G, Subpart SS, Subpart NNNNN) for the HCl-containing vent streams at your West Virginia facility.

Determine whether the hydrochloric acid scrubber is being used as an 'emission control device' subject to a subpart emission limit or instead as a 'recovery/recapture' device; identify the specific regulatory citation that designates the unit as part of the affected source.

Identify the scrubber type (water, caustic, acid-reactant) and whether it was used to demonstrate compliance in an initial performance test; gather performance test reports and the operating parameter values (flow rates, pH, temperatures) established during that test.

Verify which monitoring parameters and monitoring frequencies are currently required by the applicable subpart(s) (e.g., inlet liquid flow, recirculation flow, effluent pH, scrubbing liquid temperature, specific gravity) and whether you already record them continuously or at shift intervals.

Confirm whether a site-specific monitoring plan or Notification of Compliance Status has been or must be submitted and whether it included operating ranges based on performance test results (necessary to establish acceptable parameter ranges).

If you plan to request alternative monitoring, prepare the information required by §63.8(f) and the relevant subpart(s): identification of proposed parameter(s), justification why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, specific monitoring procedures, monitoring frequency/averaging time, supporting calculations, and demonstration schedule.

Document availability of records and measurement capability: ability to record at required intervals (e.g., continuous, once per shift, daily averages), instrumentation accuracy and calibration schedule, and procedures for data validity and handling monitoring malfunctions.

If your scrubber uses spray nozzles or a jet-ejector design, determine whether the alternative daily pressure/flow checks described in other subparts (e.g., §63.1573(b)) would be applicable and whether you can meet the response time/repair requirements for identified abnormalities.

candidates.title: Cellulose Products Manufacturing (Subpart UUUU)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a cellulose products manufacturing operation located at a major source of HAP emissions, then you are subject to this subpart

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by this subpart, then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring (OM&M) plan that addresses installation location, equipment/performance specifications, and performance evaluation procedures including calibrations

If you use a CEMS to measure hydrogen sulfide emissions for compliance with this subpart, then the CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to Performance Specification 7 (PS-7) of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B
If you use a CEMS that uses gas chromatography to measure organic HAP emissions (e.g., carbon disulfide), then the CEMS must meet Performance Specification 9 (PS-9) of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B

If you use a CPMS, then the CPMS must meet applicable performance specifications and quality assurance procedures upon promulgation and must have validation/audit devices that are NIST-traceable and at least three times as accurate as the required CPMS accuracy

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) to a monitoring requirement in a relevant standard, then you must submit an application to the Administrator and obtain approval under § 63.8(f) before relying on the alternative

If a CMS is required under the relevant standard, then that CMS is subject to the provisions of § 63.8 (including requirements for operation, maintenance, and performance evaluation) upon promulgation of applicable performance specifications

If you replace or alter monitoring methodology and the Administrator does not approve the alternative, then you remain subject to the monitoring requirements of § 63.8 and the relevant standard and must follow the specified methods

If a CMS is out of control as defined by § 63.8(c)(7), then you must take corrective action, repeat necessary tests, and exclude the out-of-control data from data averages until the CMS is back within allowable limits

If you propose an alternative monitoring procedure, then the application must describe the proposed monitoring system addressing the definition elements in § 63.2 and include a performance evaluation test plan and justification (technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality)

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: If equipment leak monitoring is performed under this subpart using a detection instrument and no instrument is available at the plant site that meets the Method 21 performance criteria, then the instrument readings may be adjusted by multiplying by the average response factor of the process fluid

If equipment is monitored for leaks under this subpart, then the instrument shall be calibrated before use on each day of its use by the procedures specified in Method 21 and calibration gases shall include zero air and specified methane (or other applicable compound) mixtures

If a piece of equipment can reasonably be expected to contain organic HAP in service, then it is presumed to be in organic HAP service unless demonstrated otherwise (percent organic HAP ≤ 5 percent by weight annually), using Method 18 or ASTM D6420-18 as specified

candidates.title: Monitoring Alternatives (Subpart GGGGG)

criteria.criterion: If you elect to use a CEMS as an alternative to the parametric monitoring required in this subpart to measure control device outlet total organic or organic HAP emissions, then the CEMS must include diluent gas monitoring (O2 or CO2) for combustion controls and complete one cycle of operation at least every 15 minutes

If you use a CEMS as the alternative monitoring method, then you must conduct a performance evaluation of the CEMS according to § 63.8 and Performance Specification 8 (for TOC CEMS) or Performance Specification 9 (for HAP CEMS) and Performance Specification 3 for O2/CO2
If you choose CEMS as an alternative, then you must prepare and follow a site-specific monitoring plan for operating, calibrating, and verifying the CEMS consistent with § 63.8(c), (d), and (e)

checklist: Confirm the facility is a cellulose food casing operation and whether the plant is a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP).
Identify whether the current GC/PID and the proposed Baseline‑MOCON Model 8900 are used as a CMS (CEMS/CPMS/COMS) for compliance or for leak detection (Method 21-style surveys).
Determine whether H2S and carbon disulfide measurements are used to demonstrate compliance with a numeric limit or as parametric/operating-limit monitoring for a control device outlet.

Verify whether the Baseline‑MOCON Model 8900 meets the relevant performance specification(s) (PS‑7 for H2S; PS‑9 for GC-based organic HAP CEMS) or whether it would be an alternative method requiring Administrator approval.
Assemble the existing site-specific OM&M / performance evaluation plan and check whether it already documents minor changes or allows the specific calibration approach you plan to use.

If proposing the instrument as an alternative monitoring method, prepare an application with: (a) description addressing the elements of monitoring per §63.2, (b) a site-specific performance evaluation test plan per §63.8(e)(3), and (c) justification (technical/economic) per §63.8(f)(4)(ii).

Confirm calibration procedures and frequency (daily calibration, zero/span checks), whether calibration gases and procedures match Method 21 or the applicable PS, and whether calibration standards are NIST-traceable if required.

If the instrument will be used for Method 21-style leak detection, determine the applicable response factor approach (average stream response factor) and whether instrument readings will be adjusted per §63.180(b)(2).

Confirm data collection and averaging requirements (CEMS: ≥1 cycle/15 min and 1‑hour averages from ≥4 equally spaced data points; CPMS/CEMS data availability and out-of-control handling per §63.8 and §63.5545).
Verify whether a diluent monitor (O2 or CO2) is required when using a CEMS on a combustion control device and whether the proposed system includes it (per §63.7947(a)(1)).
Determine whether any device used for initial validation/accuracy audit meets NIST-traceability and the 'three times more accurate' requirement for CPMS audits (per §63.5545(f)(9)).

Check applicable permitting timelines and submit the alternative monitoring application at least 60 days before a performance evaluation if the alternative will serve as the performance test method (per §63.8(f)(4)(i)).

candidates.title: Performance testing requirements (General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source is required to do performance testing by a relevant standard and no waiver or extension is obtained, then the owner/operator must perform the required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date for the source.

If the owner/operator applies for and the Administrator grants a written waiver of an individual performance test under the procedures in this section, then the individual performance test requirement may be waived.

If the owner/operator validates and obtains Administrator approval to use an alternative test method following Method 301 and the notification requirements, then the owner/operator may use the alternative method in lieu of the specified test method.

If the owner/operator demonstrates by other means to the Administrator's satisfaction that the affected source is in compliance with the relevant standard, then the Administrator may waive the requirement for performance tests.

candidates.title: Performance test methods and procedures to determine initial compliance (Coatings and related operations)

criteria.criterion: If multiple emission points are vented to one common control device to meet the subpart's requirements, then only one performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance for that group of emission points.

If an emission control device controls gaseous HAP from an existing affected source that operated prior to March 11, 1994 and is equipped with inlet/outlet continuous monitors such that percent efficiency can be calculated and those CEMs are used to demonstrate continuous compliance per the subpart, then that control device does not need to be performance tested.

If affected HAP emission points are located in an area with other gaseous emission sources not affected by the subpart and a gaseous emission test is required, then during the performance test the owner/operator must isolate the affected HAP emission points by building a temporary total enclosure or by shutting down all gaseous emission points not affected by the subpart and venting all ventilation air through stacks suitable for testing.

If the conditions of §63.7(e)(2)(iv) (waiver because compliance can be shown by other means) or §63.7(h) (waiver application procedures) are met, then an owner/operator is not required to conduct an initial performance test under this subpart.

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and waivers and alternatives (Waivers and alternative monitoring)

criteria.criterion: If the source is meeting the relevant standards on a continuous basis, or is being operated under an extension of compliance, or the owner/operator has requested an extension and the Administrator is still considering that request, then individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator.

If the owner/operator requests a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test date (unless a site-specific test plan is submitted) and must include information justifying the waiver such as technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality.

If the owner/operator demonstrates that required monitoring would not provide accurate measurements due to interferences or that the effluent from a single affected source or combined effluent is released through more than one point, then the Administrator may approve alternative monitoring methods or requirements upon written application.

candidates.title: Requirements for electric arc furnaces and AOD vessels (EAF/AOD performance testing)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an EAF or AOD vessel, then you must install, operate, and maintain a capture system that conveys collected emissions to a control device for removal of particulate matter.

If an EAF or AOD is subject to the emissions limits in paragraphs (b) or (c) of this section and no applicable exception applies, then you must conduct performance tests to demonstrate initial compliance with the applicable emissions limit for each emissions source.

If emissions from any EAF or AOD vessel are combined with emissions from facilities not subject to this subpart, then you must notify and receive approval from the Administrator for the procedures that will be used to determine compliance.

If an existing affected source has a prior performance test conducted within 5 years of the compliance date using the specified methods and the test was representative of current/anticipated operations, then the owner/operator may certify initial compliance based on the prior test in lieu of conducting a new initial performance test.

checklist: Identify which NESHAP subpart(s) are applicable to your facility (confirm whether argon stir stations and the ladle metallurgical furnace are regulated under 40 CFR part 63 Subpart YYYYY for EAF/AOD or under a different subpart).

Determine whether the argon stir stations and the ladle metallurgical furnace emissions are vented to the same baghouse (a single common control device) or to separate control devices; document ducting and control device inlet points and which emission points are routed to each compartment/stack.

If multiple emission points (argon stir stations, LMF, etc.) vent to the same control device, verify whether the subpart allows a single performance test for that group of emission points (see 40 CFR 63.705(a)).

If emissions from the argon stir stations are combined with emissions from sources not subject to the same subpart, confirm whether you must notify and obtain Administrator approval for the compliance-testing procedures (see 40 CFR 63.10686(d)(4)).

Assess whether prior performance tests exist for the baghouse or affected emission points within the past 5 years and whether those tests were conducted with the same methods and are representative of current operations (see 40 CFR 63.11466(b) and 40 CFR 63.10686(d)(6)).

Evaluate whether you can isolate the argon stir stations for testing (build a temporary total enclosure or shut down other gaseous emission points and vent all ventilation air through stacks suitable for testing) per 40 CFR 63.705(c)(2)(ii).

If testing isolation is impractical, document technical reasons (interference from co-vented sources, inability to separate emissions) and prepare justification for a waiver or alternative method application (collect technical/economic evidence per 40 CFR 63.7(h) and 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(3)).

If seeking to use an alternative test method, prepare a Method 301 validation and submit the required notification at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test (see 40 CFR 63.7(f)(2) and 40 CFR 63.7(b)).

If applying for a waiver of the performance test, prepare and submit the waiver application (and any extension-of-compliance request if applicable) at least 60 days before the test date unless the site-specific test plan is submitted (see 40 CFR 63.7(h)(3) and 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(3)).

If relying on alternative monitoring methods (e.g., because multiple effluents, moisture, or other interferences make specified CMS inaccurate), prepare an application describing the alternative and performance evaluation plan and submit to Administrator per 40 CFR 63.1112(c)(4).

Record dates and maintain timelines: 180-day testing deadlines from compliance date (unless waiver/extension granted), 60-day notification for waivers/alternative methods, and Administrator response timelines noted in the cited provisions.

Consult with the permitting authority or the EPA Administrator early (document contacts) to request approval for: (a) using prior tests, (b) alternate testing/monitoring methods, or (c) special procedures when emissions are co-vented with non-subject sources (see 40 CFR 63.10686(d)(4), 63.7(f), 63.1112(c)).

candidates.title: Control device and work practice requirements

criteria.criterion: If a flare is used to comply with applicable subparts, then the presence of the flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device to detect the presence of a flame (i.e., pilot-flame monitoring is required for flares used for compliance).

If a flare is used to comply with the provisions of this part, then the flare must be operated at all times when emissions may be vented to it and be monitored to assure operation and maintenance in conformance with its design.

candidates.title: Continuous monitoring (bulk gasoline terminal)

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator of a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1), then you must install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system as specified in § 63.427(a).

If a thermal oxidation system is used at a bulk gasoline terminal subject to § 63.422(b)(1), then a continuous parameter monitoring system capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If you wish to monitor an operating parameter other than those listed in § 63.427(a)(1)–(4) (for example, pilot-flame presence instead of firebox temperature), then you may only do so upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.422(b).

If you are subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and an alternative parameter is approved, then you must operate the vapor processing system in a manner consistent with the alternative operating parameter value and operation beyond that value constitutes a violation of the emission standard in § 63.422(b)(1).

candidates.title: Testing and monitoring requirements for bulk gasoline terminals (Subpart BBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: If your facility is a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to this subpart, then you must comply with the testing and monitoring requirements in § 63.11092, including installing/calibrating/certifying/operating/maintaining a continuous monitoring system while gasoline vapors are displaced to the vapor processor systems.

If a thermal oxidation system is used at a bulk gasoline terminal subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2, then you must install a CPMS to measure combustion zone temperature in the firebox or duct immediately downstream of the firebox but, as an alternative, you may monitor the presence of the thermal oxidation pilot flame using a heat-sensing device (e.g., UV beam sensor or thermocouple) that provides a positive/negative parameter value indicating flame on/off.

If you choose pilot-flame monitoring as the alternative for a thermal oxidation system, then the thermal oxidation system shall be equipped to automatically prevent gasoline loading operations from beginning at any time that the pilot flame is absent and you must implement the verification, maintenance, and recordkeeping requirements specified in § 63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B)(2).

If you seek to monitor an alternative operating parameter other than those listed in paragraphs (b)(1)(i)–(iii), then you may only do so upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.11088(a) and by providing the required rationale and data for the selected operating parameter value, monitoring frequency, and averaging time.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is a bulk gasoline terminal and whether the source is subject to Subpart R (i.e., subject to § 63.422(b)(1)) or Subpart BBBBBB (i.e., subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to Subpart BBBBBB).
Identify the type of vapor control device used for gasoline loading (thermal oxidation/incinerator vs. flare vs. carbon adsorption vs. refrigerated condenser).
If thermal oxidation is used, verify current monitoring: is there a CPMS temperature sensor installed in the firebox or duct immediately downstream of the firebox (before substantial heat exchange)?

If considering pilot-flame monitoring, document the specific pilot sensor type, output (positive/negative signal), and continuous-record/alarms capability and whether it can be interlocked to automatically prevent or stop gasoline loading when pilot flame is absent.

Verify whether the pilot-flame monitoring approach will include the verification, daily/periodic checks, semi-annual preventive maintenance, and written logging of alarm/shutdown events as required by § 63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B)(2) (including documentation of corrective actions and gasoline loaded estimates).

Determine whether prior performance test data exist (dates, methods used, whether combustion-zone temperature was recorded) and whether that data can be used to establish operating parameter values per § 63.11092(e)(1)(iv) and related provisions.

Confirm whether the flare (if used) meets the general requirements of 40 CFR 63.11(b) (e.g., design/operation, continuous pilot presence, monitoring) and whether the flare is subject to the § 63.11(b) provisions referenced in Subpart BBBBBB exceptions.

Verify whether any applicable state, local, or tribal enforceable rule or permit already prescribes an operating or monitoring parameter (e.g., an enforceable loading-rack limit) that could substitute for or affect the federal monitoring approach (see § 63.11092(a)(2) and related provisions).

Prepare to document and submit to the Administrator the technical rationale/data showing that pilot-flame monitoring (or other alternative parameter) demonstrates continuous compliance with the applicable emission standard, including proposed operating parameter value, monitoring frequency, averaging time, and automatic loading-prevention interlock details.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements (Steel pickling facilities and acid regeneration plants)

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then the owner/operator must perform the monitoring and performance tests required in §63.1162 and may only develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements with Administrator approval.

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device at such a facility, then the owner/operator must install, operate, and maintain continuous measurement and recording of scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate if required) and record at least once per shift while operating.

candidates.title: Monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements (Continuous monitoring systems and scrubber alternatives)

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system according to the requirements in §63.9025(a)(1)–(6).

If a scrubber is used as the control device, then you may request approval under §63.8(f) to monitor parameters other than those specified, but you must submit a monitoring plan meeting the requirements in §63.9025(b)(1)–(3) and follow the plan unless the Administrator requires an alternate scheme.
If you want to monitor alternative parameters for any other control device, then you must submit a monitoring plan to the Administrator per §63.8(f) that meets the requirements in §63.9025(c)(1)–(3).

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner/operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then you must conduct monitoring as set forth in this section and relevant sections unless the Administrator specifies minor methodological changes or approves alternatives.

If you wish to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring, recordkeeping provisions, or to monitor a different parameter than those listed, then you may request approval as provided in §63.996(d)(1)–(2) (and follow the approval procedures in the referencing subpart).

candidates.title: Monitoring alternatives (approved alternatives and how to request approval)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to monitor parameters other than those required by the subpart (including for wet scrubbers or other control devices), then you must request approval and submit a request meeting the information requirements of §63.1573(f) (description of affected source, parameter(s), justification, monitoring frequency, supporting calculations, and averaging time).

If you use an approved alternative described in this section (e.g., noncontinuous checks for pressure or pH, or other approved procedures), then you must follow the specific conditions and recordkeeping/repair timelines specified for that alternative (examples in §63.1573(b)–(d)).

checklist: Is the facility a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant that is regulated under Subpart CCC?
Is the HCl bubbler/acid absorber in question considered a wet scrubber or another type of control device under the applicable subpart(s)?

What operating parameters and operating limits were established during the most recent performance test (e.g., makeup water flow, recirculation flow, dipleg immersion depth, liquid change-out interval)?
Were the operating parameters for the control device defined during performance testing that demonstrated compliance (dates, test reports, and numeric values)?
Is continuous monitoring (CMS/CPMS) currently required by the applicable subpart or by §63.9020(e) for your source?

Can the proposed alternative limits (minimum dipleg immersion depth and maximum time between liquid change-outs) be tied to the parameter(s) that demonstrate maintenance of control efficiency during the initial performance test?
Do you have the data, test results, and supporting calculations to demonstrate that the proposed alternative monitoring will ensure ongoing compliance (including averaging time and rationale)?

Can you prepare a monitoring plan that includes: description of the control technique, test results verifying performance, the specific operating parameter(s) to monitor, monitoring procedures, frequency of measurement and recording, performance specifications, and QA/QC procedures as required by the referenced sections?
Are your monitoring devices certified/calibrated per manufacturer specs and as required (e.g., accuracy and annual calibration where specified)?

Do you have the administrative path ready to submit a request under §63.8(f) (notifications, monitoring plan, or alternative-monitoring application) to the Administrator (and any state permitting authority), and records of any prior approvals or comments relevant to alternative monitoring?

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants From Oil and Natural Gas Production Facilities (Subpart HH)

criteria.criterion: If ancillary equipment or compressors are located at a natural gas processing plant and operate in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then they are subject to the equipment leak standards of this subpart.

If ancillary equipment or compressors are subject to and controlled under the requirements of subpart H of this part or are subject to and controlled under the requirements of 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO, then the equipment leak standards in this subpart do not apply to those items.

If a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor contains or contacts a fluid with total VHAP concentration that can reasonably be expected to exceed 10.0 percent by weight, then it is presumed to be in VHAP service (unless demonstrated otherwise using the methods in § 63.772(a)).

If a potential leak interface yields an organic concentration value less than 500 parts per million by volume (according to the no detectable emissions test procedure), then that interface is determined to operate with no detectable organic emissions (i.e., no leak by this subpart's definition).

If the plant is a nonfractionating natural gas processing plant with design capacity to process less than 283,000 standard cubic meters per day, then pumps in VHAP service, valves in gas/vapor and light liquid service, and pressure relief devices in gas/vapor service at that plant are exempt from the routine monitoring requirements referenced in this section.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) — Control device and alternative work practice requirements

criteria.criterion: If an applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then the owner or operator may elect to use an optical gas imaging instrument instead of the Method 21 monitor (subject to the alternative work practice requirements in this section).

If the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) is used to identify leaks, then the owner/operator must meet the instrument specifications, daily instrument check procedures, keep video records (with date/time stamps), and perform the required annual Method 21 screening and choose a monitoring frequency from Table 1 to subpart A as specified in this section.

If the alternative work practice is used and an emission is imaged (or visible to the naked eye), then that emission is considered a leak and must be identified for repair as required in the applicable subpart and re-screened after attempted repair using either the alternative work practice or Method 21 at the leak definition required in the applicable subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Organic Hazardous Air Pollutants (Subpart H) — Test methods and monitoring (Method 21 requirements)

criteria.criterion: If monitoring is required under this subpart, then monitoring shall comply with Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, and the detection instrument must meet Method 21 performance criteria (with allowance to use an average-response-factor for the stream) and be calibrated before use each day.

If an owner/operator elects to adjust instrument readings for background when performing Method 21-style monitoring, then the background level must be determined using the same procedures and the arithmetic difference between the maximum reading and background shall be used to determine compliance.

If a piece of equipment is to be considered not in organic HAP (VOC/HAP) service under Subpart H, then the percent organic HAP content must be shown to not exceed 5 percent by weight (annual average basis) using Method 18 (or acceptable ASTM alternative) as specified.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Storage Vessels and Related Leak Inspection Provisions (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If the item is a vapor collection system, closed vent system, fixed roof, cover, or enclosure required to comply with this section, then the owner/operator must perform initial inspections per the procedures in this section (Method 21) and conduct the required annual or semi-annual visual/Method 21 inspections as specified.

If an instrument reading is greater than 500 parts per million above background (or a visual indication is observed) during these inspections, then the item is a leak and a first repair attempt must be made within 5 calendar days and repair completed within 15 calendar days (subject to allowed delay provisions).

If the owner/operator elects to adjust or not adjust instrument readings for background for these inspections, then they must follow the Method 21 background procedures and compare the arithmetic difference to 500 ppm to determine a leak.

checklist: Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant (i.e., a gas plant as defined in § 63.761).

List all ancillary equipment (pumps, valves, pressure relief devices, sampling connection systems, open-ended lines, flanges, connectors) and compressors on site and whether they are at the gas plant area subject to Subpart HH.

Determine whether each piece of ancillary equipment or compressor contains or contacts a fluid with total VHAP concentration >= 10.0 percent by weight (document using Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A or ASTM D6420 per § 63.772(a)).
For each ancillary item determined to be in VHAP service, record the number of hours per calendar year it operates in VHAP service to check the 300-hour applicability threshold in § 63.769(a).

Verify whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under Subpart H or 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOOO (if so, Subpart HH leak standards may not apply per § 63.769(b)).

If considering relying on Subpart HH exemptions, determine whether the plant is nonfractionating and whether the plant design capacity to process field gas is less than 283,000 standard cubic meters per day (to assess § 63.769(c)(5) exemption applicability).
Identify whether affected items are part of closed-vent systems, covers, fixed roofs, or vapor collection systems (Subpart G/HH inspection rules differ for these items).

Decide whether you intend to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21 and confirm you can meet the instrument specifications, daily instrument check procedures, video recordkeeping (date/time stamps), and annual Method 21 screening required by § 63.11(e) and (d).

Confirm availability of a Method 21-capable instrument or suitable calibration gas and the ability to calibrate the instrument before each day of use as required by Method 21/Subpart H (§ 63.180), or plan to use optical gas imaging and perform required daily checks and an annual Method 21 screening per § 63.11.

Prepare to keep required records and reports: VHAP determinations, inspection logs, leak detection and repair records (dates of detection, first repair attempt, repair completion or delay justification), video records for imaging, and annual Method 21 screening results as required in §§ 63.774 and 63.11.

For the ethylene glycol + water cooling-jacket service, document the fluid composition and calculate/measure total VHAP fraction to determine whether that service qualifies as VHAP service under § 63.772(a); do not assume nonvolatile glycol is non-VHAP without testing/documentation.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If required to do a performance test by a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing of the intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin.

If a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and you intend to assert it, then you must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable (and before the performance test deadline unless delayed by the force majeure), provide a written description and proposed test date, and the Administrator may approve or deny an extension to the performance test deadline in the Administrator's discretion.

If the Administrator requests review of a site-specific test plan, then you must submit the site-specific test plan to the Administrator at least 60 calendar days before the performance test (simultaneously with the notification of intent to test) or on a mutually agreed date.

If requesting a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test, then the application for the waiver must be submitted at least 60 calendar days before the performance test if the site-specific test plan is not submitted.

If you wish to change an applicable time period or postmark deadline (for example, the 60-day notification), then you must request the adjustment in writing as soon as practicable and the Administrator may approve an adjustment by mutual agreement.

If a State has been delegated authority to implement and enforce notification requirements under this part, then notifications required under this part must be submitted to the delegated State authority (and a copy to the EPA Regional Office unless the Regional Office waives that requirement).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you are required to conduct a performance test under this subpart, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin (as required by § 63.7(b)(1)).
If you are an existing affected source, then you must conduct initial performance tests no later than 180 days after the compliance date specified for your source, in accordance with § 63.7(a)(2).

If you intend to use results of a previously-conducted emission test in lieu of an initial performance test, then you must demonstrate to the Administrator's satisfaction that no changes have been made since that test, that the test methods and operating conditions conform to this subpart, that the control device and parameter values from the prior test will be used for continuous compliance, and that the test was completed within the last 60 months, and submit those test data with the Notification of Compliance Status.
If you conduct a performance test under this subpart, then the performance test must be conducted under normal operating conditions and not during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction.

If you conduct initial compliance testing under this subpart, then you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status including the performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test.

candidates.title: Subpart AAAAAAA notification/recordkeeping/reporting requirements

criteria.criterion: If you are required to conduct a compliance (performance) test under this subpart, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the compliance test at least 60 calendar days before the compliance test is scheduled to begin.

If you are using data from a previously-conducted emission test in lieu of the initial compliance test, then you must submit the test data in lieu of the initial compliance test results with the Notification of Compliance Status.

If you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status with compliance test results under this subpart, then you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status including the compliance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the compliance test.

checklist: Determine which NESHAP subpart(s) apply to your facility (e.g., Subpart LLLLL and/or Subpart AAAAAAA) and confirm the applicable relevant standard citation.

Confirm whether an initial or subsequent performance (compliance) test is required for your affected unit(s) and the applicable due date for initial testing (e.g., 180 days after compliance date/startup per 63.8686).
Identify the planned performance test date(s) and calculate the 60-calendar-day notification deadline.

Verify whether the State of Oregon is delegated for notification/reporting for the applicable subpart(s) (so you know whether to notify the State or EPA Regional Office and whether to send a copy to EPA).

If planning to use a previously-conducted emission test instead of a new test, confirm the prior test was completed within the last 60 months, that no process/control changes have occurred since that test, and assemble documentation to demonstrate conformity with the subpart (per 63.8686(b) / 63.11564(a)(6)).

If you intend to request a waiver of the performance test, prepare the waiver application and justification (technical/economic/impracticality) and note that the waiver application must be submitted at least 60 days before the test if no site-specific test plan is submitted (per 63.7(h)).

If asserting or anticipating force majeure that would delay testing, prepare written notification and supporting explanation to the Administrator as soon as practicable and identify a proposed new test date (per 63.7(a)(4)).

If submitting a site-specific test plan (or the Administrator has requested one), prepare and be ready to submit it at least 60 days before the test (or on a mutually agreed date) and be prepared for possible Administrator review/approval timeframes (per 63.7(c)(2)(iv) and 63.7(c)(3)).

If you plan to use an alternative test method (including Method 301 validation), prepare the alternative method validation and notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test (per 63.7(f)(2)(i)-(iii)).

Plan logistics to assemble and submit the Notification of Compliance Status and performance test results within 60 days after test completion, including who will compile records and whether any CBI handling is needed (per 63.8692(e) / 63.11564(a)(5)).

If seeking an adjustment to the 60-day notification requirement, prepare a written adjustment request with supporting information to submit to the Administrator as soon as practicable and be prepared to negotiate mutual agreement (per 63.9(i)(2)-(3)).

Confirm availability of required QA items for the test (e.g., audit samples, AASP availability) and that tests will be run under representative normal operating conditions (not during startup/shutdown/malfunction) per subpart test method requirements (per 63.7(c) and 63.8687(b)).

candidates.title: Subpart F — General provisions; heat exchange system requirements

criteria.criterion: If you monitor cooling water for leaks under §63.104(b) (monitoring for organic HAP, TOC, speciated HAP, or other representative substances), then the concentration must be determined using any EPA-approved method listed in part 136 that is sensitive to concentrations as low as 10 ppm and the same method must be used for both entrance and exit samples (alternative methods may be used only upon approval by the Administrator).

If you collect entrance and exit samples for a heat exchange system under §63.104(b)(4)–(b)(5), then you must collect a minimum of three sets of samples at each entrance and exit and calculate the mean entrance and exit concentrations (with corrections for makeup water or evaporative losses as applicable).

If you intend to use a sampling technique or analytical approach different from the specified part 136 methods or the Modified El Paso/stripping approach for heat exchange monitoring, then you may only use an alternative method upon approval by the Administrator as provided in §63.104(b)(3).

If you monitor total strippable hydrocarbons per §63.104(g) (Modified El Paso method option), then you must determine the stripping-gas concentration using the Air Stripping Method (Modified El Paso Method) and an FID analyzer for on-site determination as described in that method (with conversion/calculation steps specified in §63.104(g)(3) and (g)(4)).

candidates.title: Subpart G — Process vents, transfer operations, and wastewater: monitoring and test method requirements

criteria.criterion: If you are measuring vent stream concentration using Method 18 (or Method 25A where allowed) for process vent group determination or performance tests under §63.115 and §63.116, then the minimum sampling time for each run is 1 hour and you must take either an integrated sample or four grab samples (and if grab sampling is used, take the grab samples at approximately equal time intervals during the run).

If you conduct performance testing for transfer operations or shared control devices under §63.128 (and related performance-test procedures), then each run must represent at least a 1-hour period and you must use either integrated sampling or a minimum of four grab samples (with grab samples taken at approximately equal intervals) unless an allowed exception applies.

If you are performing wastewater performance tests or inlet/outlet concentration measurements under §63.145 (noncombustion or nonbiological treatment processes, combustion treatment processes, or biological treatment processes), then samples may be either grab samples or composite samples and shall be taken at approximately equally spaced time intervals over a 1-hour period with each 1-hour period constituting a run and a minimum of three runs required.

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those specified for process vents or recovery devices in §63.114(a)–(b), then you must request approval for alternative monitoring per the submission/approval mechanism referenced in §63.114(c).

checklist: Identify whether the measurement is for a heat exchange system cooling-water monitoring (Subpart F §63.104) or for a process vent/transfer operation/performance test or wastewater performance test (Subpart G §§63.115, 63.116, 63.128, 63.145).

Determine which EPA reference method you plan to use (e.g., Method 18, Method 25A, Method 320, Modified El Paso/stripping method, or a part 136 wastewater method) and read that method's sample-type allowances (integrated, grab, composite) and required sampling duration.

For heat exchange system monitoring under §63.104(b): verify that the analytical method is listed in 40 CFR part 136, is sensitive to 10 ppm, and that the same method will be used for entrance and exit samples.

For heat exchange system monitoring: confirm you will collect a minimum of three sets of entrance and exit samples as required by §63.104(b)(5), and whether those sets as collected meet the method-specific requirements (e.g., integrated vs grab).

For process vent or control-device performance tests under §§63.115, 63.116, 63.128: confirm that each run is ≥1 hour and that you will collect either an integrated sample or four grab samples at approximately equal intervals; determine whether the test method allows composite or integrated sampling in lieu of grab samples.

For wastewater performance tests under §63.145: confirm that composite samples are explicitly allowed for the wastewater option, that samples will be taken at approximately equally spaced intervals over a 1-hour run, and that you will perform a minimum of three runs.

If you want to substitute composite sampling where the rule explicitly requires grab samples or specifies 'either integrated or grab' for a gas-phase performance test, prepare to request Administrator approval for an alternative method or monitoring approach as allowed under §63.104(b)(3) (heat exchange) or the approval process referenced in §63.114(c) (process vents).

Document and retain the sampling plan and method validation/QA records showing whether the chosen sampling approach (composite vs grab/integrated) meets the specified test method requirements and whether any Administrator approval or Method 301 validation is needed.

Confirm whether your system or streams are subject to any additional specific-method sampling constraints (e.g., Modified El Paso method requirements in §63.104(g) or Method 18/25A run/interval requirements in §63.115/63.116) that would affect the acceptability of composite samples.

If proposing an alternative sampling approach, assemble the technical justification demonstrating equivalence (method detection, representativeness, timing, preservative and handling procedures) and the specific regulatory citation(s) from these subparts to support an Administrator approval request.
